The role of crowding and decision comfort during sales periods
latest.abstract: Purpose Sales periods simultaneously attract consumers through price reductions and trigger avoidance behaviors: a paradox this study addresses by examining decision comfort as a potential mediator of the effects of human and spatial crowding on visit postponement and store-switching. Gender is also examined as a moderator of these relationships. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative approach was adopted, with data collected from 378 consumers in France during official sales periods across several retail locations. The conceptual model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine relationships among perceived crowding, decision comfort, visit postponement, and store-switching. Multi-group analysis assessed gender differences. Findings Both human and spatial crowding were negatively associated with decision comfort. Lower decision comfort was associated with higher levels of visit postponement and, less robustly, with store-switching. The indirect effect of spatial crowding on visit postponement through decision comfort was supported; the indirect effects of human crowding on both avoidance behaviors were also supported but modest in magnitude, whereas the indirect effect of spatial crowding on store-switching was not supported. Gender differences were detected in the crowding–decision comfort relationships, whereas no gender differences were detected in the decision comfort–avoidance paths. Originality/value This research contributes to the marketing literature by showing that the mediating role of decision comfort depends on the form of crowding and the avoidance response considered. It extends the application of decision comfort as an emerging construct in the retail context, offering new insights into how crowding shapes consumer decision-makin

latest.title: To What Extent Does the Layout of a Departmental Store Affect Consumer Decision Fatigue?
latest.venue: Reinvention an International Journal of Undergraduate Research
latest.abstract: A departmental store layout and product placement shape the consumer decision-making process. This paper begins by charting the psychological flow of decision making and identifying the critical points that lead to decision fatigue, a cognitive stage where repeated or complex choices exhaust mental resources and lead to suboptimal decisions. This paper further aims to provide a nuanced understanding of how the retail environment of a department store influences consumer behaviour and cognitive load. Three types of store layouts are analysed: free form, grid and racetrack. A free-form layout allows the consumer to explore products and integrates various departments together for higher sales; this configuration causes comparatively high levels of decision fatigue among consumers as it encourages browsing and they are left to navigate products by themselves. A grid layout eases the navigation process by arranging aisles in a parallel structure. However, retailers can achieve the best shopping experience with low levels of decision fatigue among shoppers by implementing a racetrack layout, which not only reduces the need for consumers to decide their path but also reduces cognitive overload by guiding the consumer along one main aisle.

latest.title: Spatial optimization of vaccine supply networks in complex terrains: balancing economic feasibility and public health equity
latest.abstract: Background Vaccine supply planning in hazard-prone terrains faces compounding geographic, socioeconomic, and operational barriers. Conventional models relying on planar distances and static metrics often fail to capture true accessibility disparities, often driving inefficient infrastructure allocation and exacerbating health inequities. Purpose This study develops an integrated decision-making framework coupling spatial equity, economic feasibility, and multi-scenario resilience to systematically reconfigure the vaccine supply network across 183 counties in Sichuan, China. Methods Using high-resolution road network data from the AMap Application Programming Interface (API), we model actual geographic impedance based on travel time. An adapted two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) method, embedded with socioeconomic vulnerability indicators, pinpoints baseline accessibility disparities. Candidate hubs are selected via entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) combined with spatial-equity quotas, and a candidate-pool capacity-sufficiency check (α coefficient) determines the final candidate-pool size. A multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MO-MILP) model then co-optimizes hub configuration, capacity scaling, and cross-regional dispatch, endogenously balancing operational efficiency, equity penalties, and capacity expansion costs. Results Under entropy-weighted TOPSIS ranking with spatial-equity quotas, the initial 61-hub pool (including 21 existing CDC anchors) provides aggregate capacity equal to 82% of total demand. latest.title: The Effect of Niche Perfume Selection Attributes on the Consume Happiness: The Moderating Effect of Generation through Multi-Group Analysis
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: Niche perfume has emerged as a mainstream segment of the perfume market, moving beyond mass-market offerings by reflecting Millennials and Generation Z’s strong preference for individuality and distinctive scent identities. This study aims to analyze the effects of niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. In addition, Millennials and Generation Z are proposed as a moderator affecting the niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. An online survey targeted Korean women from Millennials and Generation Z who have experience using niche perfume. A total of 296 survey responses were analyzed using structural equation modeling with AMOS 26.0 and SPSS 25.0. The results revealed that four key selection attributes emerged from the analysis: trend orientation, brand awareness, premium price perception, and scent. In addition, scent, brand awareness, and premium price perception had significant effects on consumer happiness. Furthermore, the moderating effect of generation was confirmed through multi-group analysis. Specifically, Among Millennials, trend orientation, brand awareness, and premium price perception influenced consumer happiness, whereas scent was the most influential factor among Generation Z. By identifying these causal relationships, this study contributes to expanding the advancement of research on niche perfume and provides implications for developing differentiated strategies tailored to generational characteristics of the Millennials and Generation Z.

latest.title: The Relationship Between Perceived Value of Beauty Curation Commerce and Consumer Behavior: The Mediating Effect of Brand Awareness
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: This study systematically investigates the structural relationships between the perceived value dimensions (convenience, choice, and customization) of beauty curation commerce and consumer behavior (purchase and recommendation intentions), while examining the mediating mechanism of brand awareness. Empirical data were collected from 320 adult consumers with actual experience in beauty curation commerce and analyzed using SPSS 25.0 software to perform frequency, factor, reliability, correlation, and multi-step regression analyses. The results indicate that convenience, choice, and customization significantly enhance brand awareness, with customization identified as the primary determinant. In terms of direct influence on consumer behavior, customization and convenience positively affect both purchase and recommendation intentions, whereas choice options yield no statistically significant direct impact. Furthermore, brand awareness acts as a critical cognitive bridge, partially mediating the relationship between convenience/customization and consumer behavior, while fully mediating the relationship between choice option and consumer behavior. Academically, this research demonstrates that reducing cognitive search fatigue through convenience and personalized curation is far more effective than simply expanding product variety. Practically, beauty platform marketers must pivot from traditional inventory-listing strategies to ultra-personalized solutions, such as AI-driven skin diagnostics and streamlined purchasing interfaces, to build brand equity and cultivate long-term customer relationships, thereby securing a sustainable competitive advantage in the rapidly evolving beauty tech industry.

latest.title: Green strategy and firm performance: The mediating role of competitive advantage in emerging economy SMEs
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractSustainability transitions are a strategic imperative for SMEs in emerging economies, where institutional and resource constraints limit the direct translation of environmental strategies into performance outcomes. This study explores how green marketing and eco-innovation are associated with business performance through competitive advantage. Data were collected through a quantitative cross-sectional survey, yielding 474 valid questionnaires from owners, managers, and specialists of Vietnamese SMEs in the consumer goods sector. Environmental regulation strengthens the green marketing–competitive advantage relationship, and customer green awareness and market dynamics positively moderate the competitive advantage–performance relationship. The findings showed positive associations of eco-innovation (β = .597, p < .001) and green marketing (β = .230, p < .001) with competitive advantage, which was positively associated with business performance (β = .461, p < .001). The corresponding indirect effects through competitive advantage were significant (β = .275 and .106, respectively; both p < .001), while environmental regulation (β = .164), customer green awareness (β = .083), and market dynamics (β = .091) showed positive moderating effects. The cross-sectional design, non-probability sampling, and industry-specific focus may limit this study’s scope and generalizability in broader contexts. This study advances the sustainability and strategic management literature by providing a mechanism-based account of how environmental strategy, when extended from the Natural Resource-Based View and translated into competitive positioning, generates economic gains for SMEs in resource-constrained emerging economies.AcknowledgmentsThis articl

latest.title: Ambient lighting and basket construction in an immersive supermarket
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Retailers use store atmospherics to influence how shoppers construct baskets, yet isolating and testing atmospheric effects in operating stores is costly and difficult to standardize. Across two studies, this research examines whether an ambient lighting configuration alters basket size. Study 1 used an immersive virtual reality supermarket and showed that bright (vs. dim) lighting increased basket size and raised the basket-level Nutri-Score total, with no reliable difference in average Nutri-Score per item. Study 2 conceptually replicated the basket-size effect in a larger online sample using video and product images from the same virtual supermarket. Bright lighting again increased basket size but neither the basket-level Nutri-Score total nor average Nutri-Score per item differed reliably. Across both studies, bright lighting increased how many products shoppers selected without reliable evidence that the average selected product had a less favorable Nutri-Score. Together, the studies show that a digitally rendered ambient lighting configuration can affect basket size across two virtual-store implementations. Virtual supermarkets can therefore serve as controlled testbeds for early-stage evaluation of programmable atmospherics and basket-level outcomes.

latest.title: Algılanan Satın Alma Engellerinin Çevrimiçi İkinci El Giysi Satın Alma Niyetindeki Rolü
latest.abstract: Bu çalışma, Türkiye’deki tüketicilerin çevrimiçi ikinci el giysi pazarındaki satın alma engellerine yönelik algılarını belirlemeyi ve bu engellerin satın alma niyeti üzerindeki rolünü ortaya koymayı amaçlamaktadır. Çalışmada öncelikle ikinci el giysi tüketimi ve çevrimiçi ikinci el tüketim literatüründe tanımlanan farklı engel boyutlarından yola çıkılarak, çevrimiçi ikinci el giysi tüketimine özgü engellere ait bir çerçeve oluşturulmuştur. Çalışmada hem çevrimiçi bağlamı hem de giysi kategorisinin yapısal özelliklerini dikkate alan kontaminasyon etkisi, ürünün düşük güvenilirliği, zaman ve çaba, aşınma ve yıpranma, utanç ve çevrimiçi mağazalara yönelik güven eksikliği olmak üzere altı temel engel boyutundan oluşan bu çerçeveden yararlanılmıştır. Ardından çalışmanın amacı doğrultusunda çevrimiçi anket yöntemiyle 18 yaş ve üzeri 397 katılımcıdan elde edilen veriler, çoklu regresyon analizi kullanılarak sınanmıştır. Bulgular, çevrimiçi ikinci el giysi satın alma niyetinin özellikle kontaminasyon etkisi, aşınma ve yıpranma ile çevrimiçi mağazalara yönelik güven eksikliği algıları ile aralarında anlamlı ve negatif yönlü ilişkiler bulunduğunu göstermektedir. Buna karşılık, zaman ve çaba ile ürünün düşük güvenilirliğine ilişkin algılar görece yüksek düzeyde olmasına rağmen, bu değişkenler ile çevrimiçi ikinci el giysi satın alma niyeti arasında istatistiksel olarak anlamlı bir ilişki bulunmadığı tespit edilmiştir. Araştırma sonuçları, çevrimiçi ikinci el platformlarının güven inşası ve ürün bilgisi şeffaflığına yönelik stratejiler geliştirmesinin, Türkiye’de ikinci el giysi tüketiminin yaygınlaşmasına katkı sağlayabileceğini ortaya koymaktadır. latest.title: ЦИФРОВА МОНЕТИЗАЦІЯ МІЖНАРОДНОЇ ТОРГІВЛІ КРІЗЬ ПРИЗМУ СПОЖИВЧИХ РІШЕНЬ
latest.abstract: Стаття присвячена дослідженню механізмів цифрової монетизації міжнародної торгівлі та їх впливу на споживчі рішення в умовах розвитку цифрових ринків. Встановлено, що глобальна електронна торгівля стрімко зростає: до 2026 р. її обсяг перевищить 6,88 трлн дол. США, а цифрові послуги вже формують понад половину світового експорту. Це підтверджує трансформацію цифрової монетизації на ключовий напрям глобальної економіки. Систематизовано основні моделі монетизації (рекламну, freemium, підписну, маркетплейси, монетизацію даних) та обґрунтовано їх диференційований вплив на поведінку споживачів. Показано, що freemium-модель створює бар’єри конкуренції, а підписна — формує інерційну лояльність. Виявлено багаторівневу структуру монетизації, що охоплює транзакції, увагу, дані та лояльність. Доведено, що алгоритмічна персоналізація трансформує споживчий вибір. Визначено специфіку українського ринку в умовах воєнного стану та окреслено стратегії цифрової присутності бізнесу.

latest.title: Is impulsive buying the missing link? Family financial socialization and financial well-being among young adults in Türkiye
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Economic Studies
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the factors determining the financial well-being of university students in Türkiye within the frameworks of social learning theory and family financial socialization theory. Data collected via a survey through the YOUREPLY platform from 395 participants selected from the population using convenience sampling were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM, SmartPLS 4). Results indicate that family financial socialization is negatively related to cognitive but not affective impulsive buying, while in the main model only affective impulsive buying is significantly and negatively related to financial well-being; no indirect associations were supported in the main model. Unexpectedly, family financial socialization is negatively related to financial well-being. This pattern is primarily driven by the family financial distress dimension (β = −.463), whereas instructing money management is positively related to financial well-being (β = .191). When the five dimensions are modelled separately, cognitive impulsive buying is also positively related to financial well-being (β = .219), and one dimension-level indirect association is significant (stressing on savings → cognitive impulsive buying → financial well-being), although its sign runs opposite to the hypothesized mechanism. These results indicate that the aggregate construct masks both positive and negative dimension-level associations. To sum up, these findings point to a family financial socialization boundary condition: specific kinds of guidance behaviors are associated with more deliberative purchasing and, for money-management guidance, with greater well-being. latest.title: Socio Technical Drivers of Impulse Buying in Live Streaming Fashionpreneurship
latest.abstract: This study addresses the rapid growth of live-streaming commerce in Indonesia and its impact on impulse buying behavior within emerging digital economies. Integrating the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework with Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory, this research aims to examine how socio technical stimuli streamer factors, platform affordances, and perceived brand value, influence consumers’ emotional (shopping happiness) and cognitive (ongoing trust) states, which subsequently drive impulse buying. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data from 300 consumers who purchased local fashion products via Shopee Live and TikTok Shop. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess measurement validity and structural relationships. The results indicate that all hypothesized relationships are statistically significant. Socio-technical stimuli significantly influence both shopping happiness and ongoing trust, which in turn positively affect impulse buying, with shopping happiness emerging as the strongest predictor. This study contributes by offering an integrated socio-technical perspective on consumer behavior in live commerce and provides practical implications for enhancing engagement and trust. It also supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 8 and SDG 9, by promoting sustainable digital commerce and empowering local fashion businesses through technology-driven innovation.

latest.title: Price-Endings and Seller Signals in Online Second-Hand Retail: Evidence From a Large Consumer Marketplace
latest.abstract: Price-ending strategies such as “. 90” and “.99” are widely used in retail settings, yet little is known abouthow they operate in consumer-to-consumer online marketplaces where individual sellers, trust cues, andspatial competition shape listing behaviour. Using a large dataset from Austria’s leading online second-hand platform, we examine how price-endings relate to listing prices, seller characteristics, and localmarket structure. Sellers using rounded price-endings list items at higher prices, and these endings remainassociated with meaningful premiums. Price-ending choices also vary with local competition: sellerssurrounded by more nearby listings show different propensities to adopt particular endings. The findingscontribute to research on retail pricing and consumer decision-making by showing how psychologicalpricing interacts with trust signals and spatial competition in a digital second-hand retail environment.

latest.title: Effects of Extended Social Servicescape on Restaurant Customers' Emotions and Behavioral Intentions: Focusing on the Dimension of Meta‐Others
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT In modern eating‐out culture, consumers actively share their experiences and express their preferences through social media, with dining seen as a means of self‐expression and social interaction. Therefore, this study explores the extended social servicescape and its effects on customer emotions and behavioral intentions, introducing a new dimension of “meta‐others.” A survey of 408 South Korean restaurant consumers revealed that positive employee characteristics significantly increased (decreased) positive (negative) emotions. Within the dimension of other customers, positively displayed emotions influenced both positive and negative emotions, whereas general characteristics did not. In the dimension of meta‐others, co‐experiences enhanced (reduced) positive (negative) emotions, whereas social connectedness affected only positive emotions. Furthermore, customers' positive (negative) emotions fostered (inhibited) favorable behavioral intentions. This study offers theoretical and practical implications for understanding social dynamics in dining contexts and for designing effective service processes and marketing strategies that enhance customers' experiences and business performance.

latest.title: Bittersweet Minds, Better Selves: How Mixed Emotions Shape Preferences for Self‐Improvement Products
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Bittersweet mixed emotion—the simultaneous experience of happiness and sadness—is a common but underexplored form of mixed emotion. This research examines how bittersweet emotion shapes consumers' preferences for self‐improvement products. Across five complementary studies, including three laboratory experiments and two secondary data analyses, we show that bittersweet emotion increases preferences for self‐improvement products relative to single emotional states of happiness or sadness. We further identify perceived self‐discrepancy as the underlying mechanism: bittersweet emotion heightens awareness of the discrepancy between the actual self and the ideal self, thereby strengthening preferences for self‐improvement products. In addition, this effect is moderated by consumers' beliefs in self‐malleability. These findings advance the mixed emotions literature by highlighting the constructive role of bittersweet emotion in consumer decision making and offer practical implications for the marketing of self‐improvement products and services.

latest.title: The Role of Brand Image, Brand Ambassador, and Product Quality in Consumer Purchases of Scarlett
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to examine the effects of brand image, brand ambassador, and product quality on purchase decision among Scarlett consumers in Malang City. Design/Methodology/Approach – This study employed an explanatory quantitative approach to examine causal relationships through hypothesis testing. A total of 170 respondents were selected using purposive sampling, based on the criteria of being over 17 years old, having used Scarlett products at least once, being familiar with Scarlett’s brand ambassador, and residing in Malang City. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS Version 25. Findings – The findings indicate that brand image, brand ambassador, and product quality each have a significant effect on purchase decision among Scarlett consumers in Malang City. These results demonstrate that the three variables play an important role in influencing consumers’ decision-making when purchasing Scarlett products. Originality/Value – The study provides empirical evidence regarding the combined influence of brand image, brand ambassador, and product quality on purchase decisions in the context of a local beauty brand. The findings offer practical implications for Scarlett to strengthen its positive brand image, collaborate with popular and well-liked brand ambassadors, and continuously maintain and improve product quality to encourage consumer purchase decisions.

latest.title: From price image to online retailer loyalty: The role of trust and consumer sugrophobia
latest.abstract: This study introduces and explores sugrophobia, which is the fear of being deceived or exploited in transactions, as a key but underexplored concept influencing online shopping behavior.Sugrophobia reflects emotional discomfort stemming from self-blame and suspicion, motivating self-protective behavior.Data is collected from 600 consumers.The research hypotheses were analyzed by K-Means Cluster Analysis and SEM.As a result it was found that high sugrophobes display greater scepticism but also exhibit stronger loyalty once trust is established.Conversely, low sugrophobes are less sceptical and more responsive to price promotions.The findings reveal that trust is the primary driver of loyalty for high sugrophobes, whereas price image and trust jointly influence loyalty among low sugrophobes.

latest.title: Beyond the Individual: Rethinking Public Health Approaches to Gambling‐Related Harm
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Public health approaches to gambling‐related harm have increasingly shifted from individual pathology to population‐level frameworks. However, these approaches remain under strain, as they continue to individualize harm while attempting to address broader structural conditions. Here, we examine three dominant paradigms to show how they shape the framing of harm and the design of interventions. First, medicalization legitimizes gambling‐related harm within clinical systems but reinforces pathologized identities and professional authority. Second, stigma frameworks highlight processes of exclusion and barriers to help‐seeking but often remain insufficiently attuned to institutional and structural power. Third, structural perspectives situate harm within neoliberal governance, market expansion, and regulatory environments, yet they are unevenly translated into policy and practice. We further illustrate these tensions through the prevention paradox, which reveals a persistent mismatch between the distribution of harm and the focus of interventions. We conclude by arguing that more effective public health responses require reorienting existing frameworks toward structural accountability, with greater attention to commercial determinants, regulatory reform, and lived experience.

latest.title: A Causal Model of Factors Influencing Hospital Decisions to Use Wastewater Treatment Pond Maintenance Services in The Bangkok Metropolitan Area
latest.abstract: Research Objective: This article aimed to examine (1) the levels of service quality, 7Ps marketing mix, trust, and decision-making regarding wastewater treatment pond maintenance services among hospitals in the Bangkok Metropolitan Area and its surrounding area, (2) to develop and validate a causal model of decision-making for wastewater treatment pond maintenance services, and (3) to examine the influence of service quality, 7Ps marketing mix, and trust on hospital decision-making to use wastewater treatment pond maintenance services. Research design, data and methodology: The sample consisted of 300 personnel who were responsible for or involved in decision-making regarding wastewater treatment pond maintenance services in hospitals in Bangkok and surrounding areas. They were selected by purposive sampling. The instrument for collecting data was a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and structural equation modeling. Results: 1) The Respondents rated service quality, 7Ps marketing mix, trust, and decision-making at a high level overall. The proposed causal model demonstrated a good fit with the empirical data, showing that the measurement and structural models were proper and consistent with the theoretical framework. 2) The model proved acceptable; goodness-of-fit indices (χ²/df = 2.221, CFI = 0.973, GFI = 0.935, RMSEA = 0.064, RMR = 0.015), and the independent variables explained 72% of the variance in trust and 84% of the variance in decision-making. 3) The 7Ps marketing mix had the strongest total effect on decision-making, followed by trust and service quality. Trust significantly mediated the relationship between service quality, 7Ps marketing mix, and decision-making, confirming its crucial role as a key intervening variable

latest.title: SÜRDÜRÜLEBİLİR ADİL TİCARET: SPAR-4-SLR PROTOKOLÜ VE TCCM+ADO ÇERÇEVESİYLE SİSTEMATİK BİR DERLEME
latest.venue: Mehmet Akif Ersoy Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Enstitüsü Dergisi
latest.abstract: Bu çalışma, sürdürülebilir adil ticaret literatürünü SPAR-4-SLR protokolü (Paul vd., 2021) ve TCCM+ADO çerçevesi (Paul ve Rosado-Serrano, 2019; Paul ve Benito, 2018) temelinde sistematik biçimde derlemektedir. WoS ve Scopus veri tabanlarında gerçekleştirilen tarama sonucunda 2016-2025 dönemine ait 127 hakemli makale belirlenerek içerik analizi ve betimleyici istatistikler aracılığıyla analiz edilmiştir. Bulgular; Theory of Planned Behavior'ın hâkim teorik çerçeve olmayı sürdürdüğünü ancak teorik parçalanmışlığın yapısal bir sorun olmaya devam ettiğini, Avrupa merkezli çalışmaların coğrafi baskınlığını koruduğunu ve niyet-davranış uçurumunun alanda çözümsüz kalmaya devam ettiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Çalışma, teorik konsolidasyon, Küresel Güney ve Türkiye bağlamları ile karma yöntem tasarımlarına yönelik on araştırma önerisi sunmaktadır.

latest.title: Agentic AI Personalization in Advertising: Realizing the True Potential of N = 1
latest.abstract: With the rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI), we have come closer than ever to achieving the holy grail of personalizing advertisements to individual consumers, i.e., the ideal of N = 1. AI-driven ad serving platforms act with unprecedented agency, dynamically creating highly tailored appeals and experiences. Such “agentic AI personalization” has both positive and negative consequences. This article traces the evolution from analog personalization to agentic personalization. It then explicates the latter concept in terms of breadth, depth, and length of personalized messaging. It overviews the processes underlying agentic AI personalization and describes the dualities inherent in both its foundation and operation. Finally, it offers a theoretical framework for studying the effects of agentic AI personalization on consumer responses to advertisements, followed by an illustrative set of propositions for empirical testing.

latest.title: Emotion-linked shopping in digital media environments: a regulatory process framework with implications for adolescents and emerging adults
latest.abstract: Shopping is now embedded in social media feeds, influencer content, livestreams, entertainment, and everyday smartphone use. These hybrid media-commercial environments make browsing and purchasing readily available when distress, boredom, identity concerns, or social needs arise. Research on this topic is divided across retail therapy, compensatory consumption, impulse buying, digital emotion regulation, and compulsive buying-shopping disorder, and the presence of emotion is often treated as evidence that regulation has occurred. This critical narrative review integrates these literatures while separating emotional antecedents, regulatory intentions, changes in emotion, behavioral control, and longer-term consequences. Literature was identified through seven search sources supplemented by backward and forward citation chaining. The clearest experimental evidence concerns temporary restoration of control through choice, whereas developmental evidence is dominated by cross-sectional studies. Evidence that low-friction payment or recommender systems alter emotion-shopping sequences comes mainly from adult consumer research and general digital-commerce research and is therefore treated as indirect for adolescents and emerging adults. We develop a media-amplified regulatory-process framework in which regulatory demand is followed by shopping-affordance appraisal, enactment across multiple shopping stages, immediate and delayed outcomes, and learning that shapes later strategy selection. Regulatory narrowing is proposed as a domain-specific extension of regulatory-flexibility theory: shopping occupies an increasing share of a person’s coping repertoire as alternatives become less accessible and platform feedback makes consumption easier to repeat. latest.title: The moderating influence of economic development on the effects of ESG, customer attitude and equity in banking: a comparative study of belt and road markets
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the underexplored role of economic development in shaping customer interactions with environmental, social and governance (ESG) initiatives within banking services, using the consumer decision-making model. Design/methodology/approach This study compares customer attitudes, behaviors and equity related to ESG initiatives across belt and road markets: Hong Kong, Turkey and Africa (Kenya). Data from 817 participants (300 from Hong Kong, 245 from Turkey and 272 from Kenya) were analyzed using structural equation modeling. Findings The results show that ESG factors significantly influence customer attitudes and equity in full dataset in Turkey and Africa, while in Hong Kong, only governance factors matter. Customer attitude and equity in turn influence purchase intention in all regions. Crucially, the influence of ESG on customer perception is moderated by the level of economic development. Environmental concerns have a stronger impact in Africa and Turkey, with similar consumer responses in both countries. Governance initiatives have a stronger influence in Hong Kong. Customer attitude drives customer equity more strongly in Turkey and Africa. Practical implications These insights highlight the importance of considering economic development in ESG marketing strategies, helping marketers tailor their campaigns and enabling policymakers to develop effective ESG guidelines in diverse economic contexts across belt and road markets. This provides a better understanding of how economic development shapes ESG–consumer dynamics in banking. latest.title: Identidade em cena: cultura pop, pertencimento e decisões de compra
latest.venue: Contextus - Revista Contemporânea de Economia e Gestão
latest.abstract: Contextualização: As decisões de compra de itens vinculados à cultura POP frequentemente ultrapassam a lógica estritamente funcional, sendo orientadas por significados simbólicos, identificação com universos narrativos e vínculos afetivos. Objetivo: Esta pesquisa investigou de que modo o uso das redes sociais (URS), a nostalgia (NOST), a formação de comunidade (FC) e o vínculo com a cultura POP (VCP) influenciam o comportamento de compra (CC). Método: Os dados foram coletados por questionário online entre os meses de setembro e dezembro de 2024. A amostra foi composta por 388 respondentes válidos. Para a análise, optou-se pela Modelagem de Equações Estruturais via Mínimos Quadrados Parciais (PLS-SEM), tendo como ferramenta de apoio o software SmartPLS4. Resultados: Os resultados indicaram que o uso das redes sociais influencia positivamente a formação de comunidade e, principalmente, o vínculo com a cultura POP, enquanto o vínculo com a cultura POP se destacou como o preditor mais forte do comportamento de compra. Adicionalmente, verificou-se que o uso das redes sociais influencia o comportamento de compra tanto de forma direta quanto indiretamente por meio do vínculo com a cultura POP, ao passo que a nostalgia apresentou influência direta de menor magnitude e não sustentou efeitos indiretos via formação de comunidade ou vínculo com a cultura POP. Conclusões: Os achados reforçam a centralidade do vínculo com a cultura POP como mecanismo explicativo do consumo em ambientes digitais, ao evidenciar que o uso das redes sociais contribui para a compra principalmente quando fortalece a identificação simbólica com esse universo.

latest.title: The complementary-competitive interplay of consumer information search and experience sharing: Implications for targeted advertising and firm performance
latest.abstract: The proliferation of targeted media platforms enables firms to deliver tailored advertising to specific consumer segments, yet the heterogeneous influences of pre-purchase information search and post-purchase sharing on targeted advertising performance remain underexplored in extant research. This paper constructs a two-period symmetric duopoly game model with fully rational firms and consumers to analyze theoretical associations between two distinct consumer information behaviors and firms' equilibrium advertising and profit outcomes. We set homogeneous products, symmetric competitors, and two types of consumers (loyal buyers and comparison shoppers) to explore the strategic interplay of corporate advertising, pricing and consumer information activities. This model adopts a differentiated search cost framework: digital information access incurs zero monetary expenses, yet endogenous cognitive information overload creates non-negligible mental frictions. Search intensity s is the consumer's generic choice variable; s* denotes the endogenous equilibrium search intensity solved from consumer utility maximization (not an exogenous primitive parameter), which lies within interior range (0,1) rather than corner solution s=1. Experience‑sharing intensity e is treated as an exogenous symmetric parameter for analytical tractability. latest.title: The More Excluded, the Brighter: How Social Exclusion Experience Shapes Consumers' Preference for Brightness
latest.venue: Academic journal of management and social sciences
latest.abstract: Brightness is a core sensory cue in consumption settings, yet little is known about why consumers come to prefer bright environments under particular social-psychological states. Taking a social-interaction perspective, this research proposes that the experience of social exclusion strengthens consumers' preference for brightness: consumers who have been excluded favor brighter environments and are more likely to choose high-brightness products. The mechanism lies in perceived control. Social exclusion threatens consumers' sense of control over the environment; they then interpret brightness cues as a route to environmental mastery and rebuild control by choosing bright settings. A high sense of power further amplifies this effect. Four experiments, combining subjective evaluations with behavioral choices, support these propositions. By connecting the experience of social exclusion with consumers' preference for sensory environments, this research adds to sensory marketing theory and offers actionable guidance for practice.

latest.title: Algorithmic Pricing and Ranking: The Interplay Between Competition Law and Digital Regulation in the European Union
latest.abstract: Autonomous pricing and ranking systems create evidentiary challenges for EU competition law. Experimental research shows that independently deployed reinforcement-learning models can converge on supra-competitive outcomes without communicating, while the opacity of deep reinforcement learning complicates the assessment of algorithmic conduct. This article examines whether records and disclosures generated under EU digital regulation can strengthen the evidentiary basis for applying Articles 101 and 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union without altering the substantive requirements for liability. The study combines a review of legal and economic scholarship with a systematic interpretation of relevant legislation and case law. It examines Articles 101 and 102 TFEU, the Artificial Intelligence Act, the Digital Markets Act, the Platform-to-Business Regulation, as well as Court of Justice case law. Online travel agency markets provide an illustrative setting informed by published empirical research. The analysis distinguishes difficulties in proving concerted practices under Article 101 TFEU from difficulties in attributing ranking conduct and establishing its exclusionary effects under Article 102 TFEU. It argues that algorithmic outcomes alone cannot resolve those difficulties. Drawing on Court of Justice case law, the article develops a statutory factual benchmark: an evidentiary framework that uses applicable digital-regulatory obligations to identify relevant governance records and ranking disclosures. It distinguishes directly applicable duties from the AI Act’s contextual relevance to systems outside its high-risk categories. latest.title: IMPACT OF PRICE SENSITIVITY ON CONSUMERS’ DECISION-MAKING IN AIRLINE TICKET PURCHASES
latest.venue: Journal of Global Peace-Marketing and Communications (JGPMC)
latest.abstract: This research examines how price sensitivity shapes consumers’ decisions when purchasing airline tickets in Calabar, Cross River State. Its specific focus is on the role of alternative evaluation and sensitivity to booking time. Two null hypotheses were tested: that neither alternative evaluation nor booking-time sensitivity significantly influences ticket-purchase decisions. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, covering passengers travelling to different destinations through Margaret Ekpo International Airport. Stratified sampling was used to allocate the 400 respondents among Ibom Air, Cally Air and Air Peace. Primary data were obtained with a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, means and standard deviations) and multiple linear regression. The findings show that respondents placed the greatest emphasis on promotional deals and discounts when comparing fares (mean = 4.58), while booking early to obtain cheaper tickets was the highest-rated booking-time behaviour (mean = 3.74). Regression results indicate statistically significant effects for alternative evaluation (p = 0.004) and booking-time sensitivity (p = 0.002), both below the 0.05 threshold. The study concludes that comparing available options and choosing booking times carefully can influence ticket-purchase decisions. Airlines are therefore encouraged to review pricing arrangements and strengthen appropriate discount and promotional programmes to attract and retain customers. Keywords: Airline Ticket Purchases, Alternative Evaluation, Booking Time Sensitivity, Price Sensitivity, Consumers’ Decision-Making.

latest.title: Analisis Faktor-Faktor yang Mempengaruhi Konsumen dalam Pengambilan Keputusan Pembelian Sepeda Motor Honda di Kecamatan Keruak
latest.venue: Al-Faizi Jurnal Politik Hukum dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine whether cognitive factors, affective factors, and environmental factors influence consumers in considering purchasing decisions for Honda motorcycle products, and to identify which factor has the most dominant influence on consumers’ purchasing decisions regarding Honda motorcycle products. This study employs a qualitative research approach using descriptive data analysis. The sample was selected from the population using the accidental sampling method, resulting in a total of 100 respondents. Based on the analysis of raw data collected in the field and processed using the computerized statistical program SPSS version 16.0, the results indicate that the cognitive, affective, and environmental variables have a significant influence on purchasing decisions for Honda motorcycles in Keruak District. Furthermore, among the three variables influencing consumer purchasing decisions, the cognitive factor is the most dominant variable affecting consumers’ considerations when making purchasing decisions for Honda motorcycles in Keruak District.

latest.title: Color me aroused while keeping the cool
latest.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
latest.abstract: Abstract Drawing on visual complexity theory and the arousal properties of color, this paper challenges the prevailing assumption that only warm (longer wavelength) or highly saturated colors can induce arousal in consumers. Instead, we propose a novel pathway: multicolor logos with cool hues can elicit arousal through triggering curiosity. Across a total of eight experiments (seven preregistered with a total of 1,724 participants recruited), of which six experiments are reported in the main text, including a behavioral lab study employing biometric measures (eye tracking, galvanic skin response, pupil dilation), and three studies utilizing real product choices, we consistently find that multicolor cool logos are more arousing than single cool color designs. This heightened, curiosity-driven arousal subsequently impacts marketing outcomes, including willingness to pay and choice. These findings offer marketers alternative strategies for inducing arousal in brand communications and provide actionable guidelines for effectively designing logos.

latest.title: Determinants of the formation of the meat and sausage products market in Ukraine
latest.abstract: Purpose. The aim of this study is to identify the key determinants shaping the Ukrainian market for meat and sausage products (MSP) amid economic uncertainty, using a segment-oriented approach and analysing consumer preferences. Methodology. Primary and secondary marketing data were analysed. To identify trends in changes to consumer preferences for ready-made MSP, two surveys were conducted using Google Forms – in the pre-war period (265 respondents in 2021) and during the Russia-Ukraine war (231 respondents in 2024), using the identical set of questions. The range of fluctuations in the influence of factors on consumers’ choice of MSP was determined using an econometric model. The χ² test, Cramer’s V and φ coefficient were used to establish the degree of relationships between the variables. Results. The main factors influencing consumers’ choice of MSP in the pre-war period and during wartime are personal experience, product composition, discounts and special offers, and the price of the goods. However, recently, when purchasing MSP, consumers have placed greater importance on price and discounts, as well as product composition; there has also been an increase in their preference for smaller-weight packaged products, the search for product information online, and purchasing these items in supermarkets. For different types of MSP, which are favoured by specific market segments, producers must adopt a differentiated approach, focusing on the factors identified in this study. Producers of dry-cured sausages, cured meat products, cooked and cooked-smoked sausages, wieners and short sausages should pay particular attention to the composition of these products, whilst producers of meat rolls and pates should focus on price, which is crucial in the production and marketing o

latest.title: THE EFFECT OF INCOME LEVEL, LOAN INTEREST RATES, AND EASE OF ACCESS TO THE APP ON GENERATION Z’S DECISIONS TO USE ONLINE LOAN SERVICES IN BANDAR LAMPUNG FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF ISLAMIC FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
latest.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Accounting Research (IJEBAR)
latest.abstract: Developments in financial technology in Indonesia have made it easier to access various financial services, including online loans, which are now increasingly popular amongst Generation Z. This situation highlights the importance of understanding the factors that influence an individual’s decision to use online loans. This study aims to examine how income levels, loan interest rates, and the ease of accessing loan application platforms influence Generation Z’s decisions regarding the use of online loan services in Bandar Lampung City, from the perspective of Islamic financial management. This study employs a quantitative approach with a population of 249,770 members of Generation Z in Bandar Lampung. The sample comprised 100 respondents, selected via probability sampling using the Slovin formula with a margin of error of 10 per cent. Data were collected via a questionnaire and analysed using the PLS-SEM method with the aid of SmartPLS software.

latest.title: Privatization, ownership structure and policy trade-offs: The sale of Íslandsbanki
latest.abstract: This paper examines the three-stage privatization of the Icelandic bank Íslandsbanki in 2021–2025 as a case of how public sellers balance revenue maximization against ownership and governance objectives. Using official reports, auction documentation, order-book data, market prices and post-sale shareholder lists, the study evaluates whether discounts granted to buyers produced durable benefits in ownership structure. All three offerings were heavily oversubscribed. In the 2022 accelerated book-building (ABB) sale, demand remained many times the amount offered even at prices above the chosen sale price. Yet dispersed ownership declined after the public offerings, foreign participation remained limited, and common ownership across competing Icelandic banks became substantial. The findings suggest that discounted pricing and initial allocation are weak instruments for shaping long-run ownership when shares are freely tradable. The case contributes to corporate governance research by linking privatization design to ownership structure, institutional ownership and principal–agent problems in public asset sales.

latest.title: The Economics of Scarcity and Ecosystem Lock-in: NVIDIA's Premium Pricing, Market Power and Consumer Willingness to Pay in the AI Accelerator Market
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: This study analyzes NVIDIA's high pricing model in the AI chip market by combining the concepts of product differentiation, market power, and consumer behavior. It suggests that NVIDIA has established very high switching costs with the CUDA ecosystem, making the price elasticity of demand very low, if not approaching zero, allowing them to charge a price well above the marginal cost. While this approach is based on using excess profits to invest in technological progress, it has also brought about demand-side issues such as distortions in the allocation of resources resulting from the "computing capacity tax" and consumer surplus reductions due to hardware-and-software bundling. At the industry level, it has exacerbated the excessive concentration of the market and created systemic risks. To address this, this study recommends steps to optimize these measures, like setting up interoperable technical standards, moving towards transparent tiered-pricing regulations, and enhancing the resilience of the supply chain. These measures are designed to maintain a balance between the corporate incentives for innovation, market fairness, and efficiency, and to offer a theoretical reference for the healthy development of the AI industry ecosystem and inclusive growth in the global digital economy.

latest.title: Kadın tüketicilerin yeşil kozmetik satın alma tercihlerinin açıklanmasında LOHAS eğilimlerinin rolü
latest.abstract: Sağlıklı yaşama ve çevresel sürdürülebilirliğe yönelik duyarlılığın artması, tüketicilerin satın alma kararlarında ürünlerin kişisel ve çevresel yararlarını birlikte değerlendirmelerini önemli hâle getirmektedir. Bu araştırmanın amacı, kadın tüketicilerin Sağlıklı ve Sürdürülebilir Yaşam Tarzı (LOHAS) eğilimleri ile yeşil kozmetik satın alma tercihleri arasındaki ilişkiyi incelemektir. Araştırmanın çalışma grubunu Türkiye’de yaşayan 18 yaş ve üzerindeki 340 kadın tüketici oluşturmaktadır. Veriler, Mart–Haziran 2026 tarihleri arasında kolayda örnekleme yöntemiyle ulaşılan katılımcılardan yüz yüze anket aracılığıyla toplanmıştır. Verilerin analizinde frekans analizi, açımlayıcı faktör analizi, Pearson korelasyon analizi ile basit ve çoklu doğrusal regresyon analizlerinden yararlanılmıştır. Açımlayıcı faktör analizi sonucunda, LOHAS ölçeğinin özgün altı boyutlu yapısından farklı olarak dört faktörlü bir yapı elde edilmiştir. Zihinsel, duygusal ve ruhsal sağlık maddelerinin aynı faktör altında toplanması nedeniyle bu boyut “psikolojik sağlık” olarak adlandırılmıştır. Basit doğrusal regresyon analizi, genel LOHAS eğiliminin yeşil kozmetik satın alma tercihinin pozitif ve anlamlı bir yordayıcısı olduğunu ve satın alma tercihindeki toplam varyansın %24,3’ünü açıkladığını göstermiştir. latest.title: DETERMINANTS OF PURCHASE CHANNEL CHOICE AND THE ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY OF E-COMMERCE TOOLS FOR SMALL FOOTWEAR BUSINESSES: EVIDENCE FROM A MULTINOMIAL LOGIT MODEL IN UZBEKISTAN
latest.abstract: This study identifies the factors determining consumers' choice of footwear purchase channel (online, offline, or mixed) and evaluates the economic efficiency of e-commerce tools for small businesses in Uzbekistan's footwear industry. Using survey data collected from 501 respondents in 2026, purchase channel choice is modelled using multinomial logistic regression, with the online channel serving as the reference category. All estimates were obtained using Stata 17.0. The model is statistically significant (LR χ² = 181.62; p < 0.001; McFadden's pseudo-R² = 0.181; AIC = 936.01). Product type emerges as the strongest determinant: for slippers and everyday footwear, the relative risk of choosing the offline channel is 10.1 and 7.4 times higher, respectively. Monthly buyers are 76% less likely to choose the offline channel, while users of the Payme and Paynet payment systems demonstrate a pronounced preference for online purchasing (RRR = 0.31 and 0.28, respectively). Uncertainty regarding footwear size and fit is the primary barrier to online purchasing (41.7% of respondents). A scenario-based assessment of four priority solutions at "ZOLUSHKA STYLE" OK indicates that the least costly solutions generate the highest returns: an accurate size chart combined with visual content (ROI = 222.0%) and a Telegram bot integrated with a customer database (ROI = 168.3%). In contrast, expansion through marketplace channels yields the lowest return (ROI = 21.0%; CLV/CAC = 1.86). The combined economic effect of the four solutions amounts to UZS 36.05 million, equivalent to 39.9% of the enterprise's net profit. latest.title: Breaching take-make-dispose cycle: “Beauty in the Flawed”- a study of customers' intent to purchase upcycled fashion
latest.abstract: Introduction The global fashion industry is currently facing an environmental crisis and is being driven toward circular-economy models such as upcycling. Upcycling employs creative reuse of post-consumption superfluous materials to create higher-value offerings. Studies indicate that there is growing awareness of the ecological impact of fast fashion, but this has not diminished demand for it. Today's younger cohorts are digital natives with high levels of social self-expression and environmental awareness, yet are difficult to engage with upcycled apparel, reflecting a disconnect. Despite rising environmental awareness among younger cohorts, adoption and purchase intentions for upcycled fashion remain limited. This research aims to fill critical gaps in the understanding of upcycled fashion purchase intention among young, urban, tech-savvy consumers. Method A structured survey from 477 participants was analyzed through Structural Equation Modelling. The model also seeks to determine the moderating influence of narrative competence on the relationship between the key antecedents and customers' purchase intention, using Process Macro. Result This paper examines the key customer values—functional, social, emotional, conditional, and epistemic—and the moderating effects of Narrative competence on purchase intention for upcycled fashion. By leveraging this theoretical framework, this research aims to fill critical gaps in understanding upcycle fashion purchase intention among younger cohorts, offering valuable implications for both academia and industry. Discussion The study contributes towards developing a unified Consumer Value-Narrative competence model for studying the purchase intention in the context of upcycled fashion. latest.title: AI-Mediated Brand Selection in Riyadh's Traditional Grocery Channel
The Price of Pocket Money
latest.abstract: Adolescent consumption lies at the intersection of behavioural economics, developmental psychology and consumer research. Although conventional economic models explain consumer choice through preferences, prices and budget constraints, actual purchasing decisions may also be shaped by cognitive biases, emotional responses, peer influence and the perceived origin of money. This study examines the relationship between adolescents’ income sources and impulsive spending, with attention to parental allowances, monetary gifts, family transfers and personal earnings. Its theoretical framework draws on mental accounting, the house-money effect, psychological ownership and the pain of paying, while also considering parental financial practices, digital payments, social commerce and targeted advertising. The research uses a quantitative primary-research approach based on survey responses collected from more than 500 teenagers. The survey provides first-hand material for examining adolescents’ money sources and spending behaviour; published research is used to contextualise the topic and interpret the possible mechanisms behind consumer decisions. The paper does not assume that earned income necessarily leads to responsible spending or that unearned income inevitably produces impulsive purchases. Instead, it considers how income origin may interact with financial responsibility, perceived scarcity, budgeting practices and the contemporary consumption environment. The study’s conclusions and recommendations are framed with due regard to the limits of survey-based evidence and the need to distinguish observed associations from causal explanations.

latest.title: ANALISIS PENGARUH KONTEN PROMOSI GALAXY ROLL DI TIKTOK TERHADAP KEPUTUSAN PEMBELIAN PADA PENGGUNA TIKTOK
latest.venue: Didaktik Jurnal Ilmiah PGSD STKIP Subang
latest.abstract: The growth of social media has expanded opportunities for digital marketing communication, particularly through short-form videos on TikTok. This study examines the effect of Galaxy Roll promotional content on purchase decisions among TikTok users who have viewed the brand’s promotional content. A quantitative survey was conducted with 100 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were processed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27, including validity and reliability tests, simple linear regression, a t-test, and coefficient of determination analysis. The findings indicate a positive and statistically significant association between promotional content and purchase decisions (t = 8.994; p < .001). The regression coefficient was 0.645, and R² was 0.452, indicating that promotional content accounted for 45.2% of the variation in purchase decisions. However, the Kolmogorov–Smirnov residual normality test was significant (p = .041), suggesting that the regression inference should be interpreted with caution. The findings highlight the relevance of informative and engaging TikTok promotional content in consumer decision-making.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
