latest.title: Going Concern Assessment Reform in Bankruptcy: Preventing Premature Liquidation and Protecting Employment
latest.venue: Jurnal Pengabdian Hukum Indonesia (Indonesian Journal of Legal Community Engagement) JPHI
latest.abstract: Bankruptcy and postponement of debt repayment obligations in Indonesia face problems in the application of the going concern principle because the debtor's business sustainability has not been the basis for an objective assessment in determining restructuring or liquidation. The PKPU system, which relies on creditor voting weighted by receivable value, has the potential to entrench majority-creditor dominance and disregard the commercial viability of a debtor whose business is still worth preserving. This study aims to analyze the weaknesses of the regulation of the principle of going concern in the bankruptcy system and PKPU and formulate a reform model through the application of Going Concern Assessment System. This study uses normative legal research methods with a legislative, conceptual, and comparative legal approach through a study of settings in Indonesia, The Netherlands, Germany, the United States, and the United Kingdom. The findings indicate that Indonesian bankruptcy law has not provided an independent and objective assessment mechanism to distinguish debtors who are experiencing temporary financial difficulties from debtors who are structurally no longer fit to maintain their businesses. Therefore, it is necessary to integrate the Going Concern Assessment System within the PKPU framework based on financial condition, business prospects, recovery capabilities, and professional supervision. The reforms are expected to prevent premature liquidation, protect workers and supply chains, maintain economic value, and support the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

latest.title: The impact of ai recommendation systems on impulsive buying behaviour in electronic marketplaces: The mediating moderating role of fear of missing out
latest.venue: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence has spread rapidly across e-commerce, and in doing so it has reshaped how consumers reach purchase decisions. Scholarship to date concentrates mainly on what shoppers gain from algorithmic recommenders, whereas far fewer studies ask whether such systems also push buyers toward unplanned spending. The present work therefore tests how perceived attributes of AI recommendation engines relate to impulsive buying, treating fear of missing out (FOMO) simultaneously as an intervening variable and as a boundary condition. Survey evidence was gathered from 823 Vietnamese shoppers who regularly transact on AI-enabled marketplaces. Results show impulsive purchasing rising together with perceived AI authority, perceived task complexity, and with perceived personalization. FOMO carries a significant portion of each effect and, at the same time, amplifies its magnitude. These outcomes ground several managerial recommendations for platforms seeking to reconcile recommender deployment with responsible consumer conduct.

latest.title: THE DEVELOPMENT OF MARKETING IN TIMES OF CRISIS: CURRENT TRENDS AND PROSPECTS
latest.abstract: The article examines the peculiarities of marketing development in the context of modern crisis processes caused by global challenges, digital transformation, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the full-scale war in Ukraine. The study focuses on the analysis of changes in the marketing environment, which have influenced the formation of new approaches to strategic planning, communication with consumers, and organization of marketing activities of enterprises. The main factors affecting the transformation of marketing practices are identified, including economic instability, changes in consumer behavior, technological development, and increased uncertainty of the external environment. The article analyzes the key trends in modern marketing, including digitalization of business processes, the growing importance of social media, development of influencer marketing, implementation of artificial intelligence technologies, personalization of communications, and strengthening of socially responsible marketing approaches. Particular attention is paid to the role of digital tools, which have become essential for maintaining communication with consumers, promoting products and services, analyzing market trends, and adapting marketing strategies to changing conditions. The study examines the adaptation of Ukrainian enterprises to wartime conditions, including changes © Гаврилюк І.І., 2026 in marketing instruments, regional differences, optimization of marketing budgets, and implementation of crisis management approaches. It is determined that the war has significantly influenced consumer behavior, increasing the importance of trust, brand values, social responsibility, and emotional connection between companies and their audiences. latest.title: Same Rules, Different Outcomes: Member-State Politics and EU Regulation of Chinese Investment
latest.abstract: Since the late 2010s the European Union has assembled an expanding toolkit for regulating foreign investment, including the FDI Screening Regulation, the Foreign Subsidies Regulation and countervailing duties on battery electric vehicles from China. This article examines how that toolkit affects Chinese enterprises, whose investment in Europe rose by 67 per cent in 2025 and whose profile—pervasive state links, concentration in strategic manufacturing sectors and complex holding structures—places them at the centre of EU scrutiny. Drawing on investment data, EU legal instruments and case evidence, the article advances three arguments. First, European protectionism differs from its American counterpart in relying on regulation rather than tariffs, a choice rooted in Europe’s economic malaise and in the shift from complementarity to homogeneous competition with China. Second, because implementation rests largely with member states, domestic politics—including populist mobilisation and changes of government—shape how stringently common rules are applied; Hungary’s 2026 change of government shows how quickly a perceived gateway for Chinese capital can tighten. Third, the effects on Chinese firms operate through four mechanisms: higher entry thresholds, rising compliance costs, a shift from acquisitions towards greenfield and joint-venture investment, and relocation across member states. Chinese investment is increasingly concentrated in precisely the sectors where scrutiny is strongest. The article concludes with implications for firms, Chinese policymakers and China–EU economic dialogue, including the case for reviving the Comprehensive Agreement on Investment.

latest.title: Development of personalized machine learning models for predicting panic attacks in college students
latest.abstract: Panic attacks (PAs) are unexpected episodes of intense fear and anxiety, accompanied by cognitive and physical symptoms that significantly impair day-to-day functioning. This study proposes a machine learning approach to predict PA risk in the upcoming week in individuals across mental health conditions, enabling timely and potentially preventive mental health intervention. We evaluate the approach in a longitudinal sample of behavioral and physiological data collected using Oura rings from 39 college students over six months. We assessed multiple prediction algorithms applied within both personalized and generalized frameworks, fitting unique models for each participant and pooling data, respectively. Across all 39 participants, personalized models using logistic regression achieved a pooled PR AUC lift of 1.17 (95% CI: 1.05–1.25) over chance-level prediction ( p = .035), whereas the generalized model did not differ from chance (PR AUC lift of 0.99; 95% CI: 0.90–1.08); in a direct comparison, personalized models outperformed the generalized model (lift ratio=1.18, p = .047). Performance varied across participants: when personalized models were grouped by unsupervised clustering of test-set PR AUC lift, models clustered as well-fit ( n = 8) showed a pooled PR AUC lift of 2.26 (95% CI: 1.50–2.89) and models clustered as poor-fit ( n = 31) a lift of 1.09 (95% CI: 0.98–1.17). Because these groups were defined by test-set performance, they describe observed heterogeneity and require validation in independent data. latest.title: Employee Capabilities for Digital Service Innovation in Multi-Level Marketing: An Application of Importance - Performance Analysis(IPA)
latest.venue: Advances in management and applied economics
latest.abstract: Digital service innovation has become essential for enhancing customer value and organizational competitiveness. However, research on the capability requirements of multi-level marketing (MLM) practitioners remains limited. Drawing on Service-Dominant Logic, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, this study identifies four key capability dimensions: Persuasion, Co-creation, Adaptability, and Self-sustainability. Using questionnaire survey data and Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA), the study examines the perceived importance and actual performance of these capabilities to identify management priorities and resource allocation needs. The findings reveal gaps between capability importance and performance, highlighting areas requiring targeted improvement. This study contributes to digital service innovation research in the MLM context and offers practical insights for developing training strategies and capability-building programs to support digital transformation. JEL classification numbers: C83, M15, O31. Keywords: Multi-level Marketing (MLM), Digital Service Innovation, Employee Capabilities, Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA), Service Management.

latest.title: Spatial optimization of vaccine supply networks in complex terrains: balancing economic feasibility and public health equity
latest.abstract: Background Vaccine supply planning in hazard-prone terrains faces compounding geographic, socioeconomic, and operational barriers. Conventional models relying on planar distances and static metrics often fail to capture true accessibility disparities, often driving inefficient infrastructure allocation and exacerbating health inequities. Purpose This study develops an integrated decision-making framework coupling spatial equity, economic feasibility, and multi-scenario resilience to systematically reconfigure the vaccine supply network across 183 counties in Sichuan, China. Methods Using high-resolution road network data from the AMap Application Programming Interface (API), we model actual geographic impedance based on travel time. An adapted two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) method, embedded with socioeconomic vulnerability indicators, pinpoints baseline accessibility disparities. Candidate hubs are selected via entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) combined with spatial-equity quotas, and a candidate-pool capacity-sufficiency check (α coefficient) determines the final candidate-pool size. A multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MO-MILP) model then co-optimizes hub configuration, capacity scaling, and cross-regional dispatch, endogenously balancing operational efficiency, equity penalties, and capacity expansion costs. latest.title: Blockchain traceability investment in agricultural supply chains: cost sharing, fairness concerns, and channel performance
latest.abstract: Introduction This study investigates optimal decisions in a blockchain-enabled agricultural supply chain under alternative cost-sharing and fairness-concern configurations. Methods A two-stage Stackelberg game is developed with a manufacturer as the leader and a retailer as the follower. The manufacturer determines the wholesale price and blockchain traceability level, after which the retailer determines the retail price and marketing effort. Fairness-adjusted utilities are constructed using generalized Nash-bargaining reference profits. Four scenarios are examined: no cost sharing with fairness-neutral parties (NN), no cost sharing with a fairness-concerned manufacturer (NM), cost sharing with fairness-neutral parties (SN), and cost sharing with a fairness-concerned retailer (SR). Closed-form equilibria and comparative-static results are derived and examined numerically. Results Under fairness neutrality, retailer cost sharing reduces the manufacturer's effective investment burden and increases wholesale price, retail price, traceability level, and marketing effort. It benefits the manufacturer but reduces retailer profit at sufficiently high sharing ratios; total supply-chain profit increases only below a threshold. Without cost sharing, stronger manufacturer fairness concern raises the wholesale price but reduces traceability investment and both parties' monetary profits. Manufacturer utility may initially increase before declining beyond a critical fairness threshold. Under cost sharing, retailer fairness concern lowers the retail price, marketing effort, traceability investment, and manufacturer profit. Its effects on retailer and total supply-chain profit depend on the cost-sharing ratio, bargaining power, and fairness concern. Discussion Within the configurations

latest.title: SALES RISKS OF TRADING COMPANIES: THE INTERRELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PRODUCT POLICY, SALES POLICY AND CONSUMER BEHAVIOR
latest.abstract: The article examines the problem of identifying and managing sales risks of trading companies under an unstable market environment characterized by military threats, logistical constraints, inflationary pressures, digitalization, and transformations in consumer behavior. The purpose of the study is to substantiate the theoretical and methodological foundations for identifying and systematizing sales risks based on determining the relationship between product and sales policies and consumer behavior. The essence of sales risks is clarified as the probability of adverse deviations in the processes of forming and implementing a product offering caused by a mismatch with consumer demand, shortcomings in assortment and sales decisions, distribution channels, logistics, and product movement. Sales risks are systematized according to the areas of their occurrence and manifestation, with nine groups identified: product, logistics, marketing, pricing, communication, channel and distribution, counterparty and contractual, financial, and competitive risks. The main manifestations of these risks and their potential impact on sales volumes, inventory turnover, profitability, and financial performance are determined. Particular attention is paid to the influence of changes in consumer needs, preferences, purchasing motives, and behavioral patterns on product and sales decisions. The relationship between consumer behavior, product policy, sales policy, and sales risks is substantiated. A conceptual framework of their interaction is proposed, covering consumer needs and behavior, product offering, product risks, sales policy, sales risks, sales performance, and consumer response. The cyclical nature of this interaction is demonstrated, whereby changes in consumer needs generate market

latest.title: Consumer sustainability judgments in omnichannel luxury retail: social media engagement and perceived last-mile delivery performance in Saudi Arabia
latest.abstract: Consumers may form sustainability judgments from general brand-engagement and service-performance cues even when those cues do not directly measure sustainability communication or environmental performance. This study examines the associations of social media engagement (SME) and perceived last-mile delivery performance (LMD), operationalized as respondent-reported delivery-performance perceptions, with customer satisfaction, consumer sustainability perception, and attitudinal brand loyalty in Saudi omnichannel luxury retail, while testing digital literacy and brand perception as moderators of the SME–sustainability association. A cross-sectional English-language survey conducted in Jeddah and Riyadh yielded 900 completed submissions; sequential eligibility screening followed by a post-eligibility response-quality review produced a primary analytical sample of 384. The survey did not separately verify personal receipt of a focal-brand delivery or the informational source underlying each LMD rating; accordingly, LMD may combine experience-based evaluations with inferred or halo-based brand beliefs. The scoring strategy uses compatible response formats: CS1–CS4 for satisfaction, S1–S3 for sustainability perception, BL1–BL3 for loyalty, SME1–SME2 for social media engagement, and LE1–LE3 for delivery-performance perception; binary CS5 and SME3 are analyzed separately rather than combined with the Likert composites. All hypotheses were estimated using HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust inference. In the primary N = 384 analysis, SME was positively associated with satisfaction ( β =.277, p < .001) and loyalty ( β = .351, p < .001), but not with sustainability perception ( β = .136, p = .084). LMD was positively associated with satisfaction ( β = .199, p = .023), sustainability per

latest.title: Strategic Leadership and Organizational Agility of Micro Start-Up Enterprises in Region XII Towards Industry 4.0 Readiness
latest.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS
latest.abstract: This study assessed the Industry 4.0 preparedness of micro start-up enterprises in Region XII (SOCCSKSARGEN) with a focus on strategic leadership and organizational agility. Based on Strategic Leadership Theory, Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Industry 4.0 Readiness Model, the study investigated organizational capabilities that enable firms to respond to technological and market changes. The study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design involving micro start-up enterprises in the region. The respondents were owners, co-founders or managers and data was collected through structured questionnaires. The levels of strategic leadership, organizational agility and Industry 4.0 readiness were determined through descriptive statistics, tests of significant differences and multiple regression analysis to examine the predictive contribution of the organizational variables. The results showed that strategic leadership and organizational agility were Highly Practiced, and Industry 4.0 readiness was Moderately Ready. Environmental Scanning was relatively a lower dimension of strategic leadership while flexibility and operational speed was relatively a lower dimension of organizational agility. Least mature dimension of Industry 4.0 readiness was Data-Driven Decision Making. Regression analysis showed that organizational agility significantly predicted Industry 4.0 readiness, but strategic leadership did not make a significant unique contribution when both variables were considered simultaneously. Based on these findings, the Strategic Agility and Industry 4.0 Readiness Enhancement (SAIRE) Framework was proposed to strengthen environmental scanning, leadership capability, organizational flexibility, operational speed, digital transformation and data-driv
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Executive Technical Backgrounds, Strategic Attention, and Digital Transformation: Evidence from a Longitudinal Case Study of Haier Smart Home
latest.venue: Asia-pacific Journal of Convergent Research Interchange
latest.abstract: This paper investigates the strategic pathways for the digital transformation of manufacturing enterprises through a longitudinal case study of Haier Smart Home.Against the backdrop of rapid technological advancement and industrial upgrading, the study explores how the characteristics of the Top Management Team (TMT), particularly their technical backgrounds, appear to shape the direction and effectiveness of digital transformation strategies.Drawing upon Upper Echelons Theory and the attention-based perspective, the research examines the dynamic relationship between executive backgrounds, strategic attention allocation, and organizational transformation over 13 years.To achieve this objective, the study adopts a mixed-methods approach that combines TMT résumé analysis, text mining of annual reports, and financial indicator analysis.First, the study systematically analyzed senior executives'educational and professional backgrounds to identify how technical expertise evolved within the leadership structure.Second, annual reports spanning more than a decade were processed using text mining techniques to trace shifts in strategic attention toward digitalization, smart manufacturing, and innovation-related themes.Finally, financial performance indicators were examined to assess patterns in the economic outcomes that coincided with strategic transformation.The findings suggest that upper-echelon executive's technical orientation is associated with disclosed strategic emphasis.More importantly, shifts in strategic attention emerge as a potential explanatory pathway linking TMT characteristics to enterprise digital transformation strategies.The study further indicates that firms with technically oriented executives exhibit more pronounced digital transformation patterns and mo

latest.title: The Relationship Between Perceived Value of Beauty Curation Commerce and Consumer Behavior: The Mediating Effect of Brand Awareness
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: This study systematically investigates the structural relationships between the perceived value dimensions (convenience, choice, and customization) of beauty curation commerce and consumer behavior (purchase and recommendation intentions), while examining the mediating mechanism of brand awareness. Empirical data were collected from 320 adult consumers with actual experience in beauty curation commerce and analyzed using SPSS 25.0 software to perform frequency, factor, reliability, correlation, and multi-step regression analyses. The results indicate that convenience, choice, and customization significantly enhance brand awareness, with customization identified as the primary determinant. In terms of direct influence on consumer behavior, customization and convenience positively affect both purchase and recommendation intentions, whereas choice options yield no statistically significant direct impact. Furthermore, brand awareness acts as a critical cognitive bridge, partially mediating the relationship between convenience/customization and consumer behavior, while fully mediating the relationship between choice option and consumer behavior. Academically, this research demonstrates that reducing cognitive search fatigue through convenience and personalized curation is far more effective than simply expanding product variety. Practically, beauty platform marketers must pivot from traditional inventory-listing strategies to ultra-personalized solutions, such as AI-driven skin diagnostics and streamlined purchasing interfaces, to build brand equity and cultivate long-term customer relationships, thereby securing a sustainable competitive advantage in the rapidly evolving beauty tech industry.

latest.title: Stakeholder Engagement and Organizational Agility On Quality Service: Strategic Governance Program Stakeholder Engagement and Organizational
latest.abstract: This study aims to assess the effect of organizational agility and Stakeholder engagement on the service quality in the Roble Shipping Co, at North Rec., Cebu City during Calendar Year 2026 towards Strategic Governance Program. Descriptive survey was used to gather data about varying subjects. There were 100 respondents in this research composing of ten (10) employees, fifty (50) Passengers and forty (40) shippers and were chosen in random. These client respondents avail the services of the company. Overall, the findings demonstrate a consistent pattern in which all dimensions of quality service delivery significantly affect all dimensions of quality service status. The major gap identified in this study lies in the difference between the company's acceptable customer perceptions and the moderate implementation of its service delivery practices. This finding suggests that existing operational systems may not yet be maximizing their potential to provide excellent customer experiences. In conclusion, the company should strengthen response management systems, establish clearer service standards, enhance schedule monitoring, improve customer communication channels, and provide continuous employee development programs focusing on customer relations and service efficiency. Based on the findings, the null hypothesis is rejected since all p-values (0.00%–0.17%) are lower than the 5.00% level of significance. Therefore, there is a significant relationship between the extent of quality service delivery and the status of quality service of the company. Based on the conclusions reached in the service quality in the Roble Shipping Co, at North Rec., Cebu City during Calendar Year 2026 is highly recommended that Strategic Governance Program be considered for implementation.

latest.title: In Value Creation: The Mediating Roles of Lean Sustainability and Sustainable Quality Culture in Linking Values‐Based Leadership to Organizational Outcomes
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This research investigates the mechanisms by which value‐based leadership (VBL) impacts critical organizational outcomes, namely, operational performance (OPP), business performance (BSP), and business survival (BSV). Specifically, it examines the mediating roles of lean sustainability (LES) and sustainable quality culture (SQC) in translating leadership into tangible results. The research employs a quantitative research design using survey data collected from 402 middle and senior‐level managers. The proposed research model and hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) with SmartPLS 4. A two‐stage analytical approach was followed, involving the evaluation of the measurement model (reliability and validity) and the structural model (path coefficients and mediating effects). The direct effect of values‐based leadership on sustainable quality culture (β = 0.759; t = 26.912; p < 0.001) was identified as the strongest relationship in the model. In the mediation analysis, the indirect effect of values‐based leadership on lean sustainability through sustainable quality culture (β = 0.395; t = 12.494; p < 0.001) emerged as the most prominent mediation mechanism. All seven proposed hypotheses (between H1 and H7) were statistically supported, with coefficients excluding zero within the 95% confidence interval and significance levels of p < 0.001. While the research uses a robust sample of 402 managers, the use of non‐probability purposive sampling may limit generalizability. Future research could adopt longitudinal designs to further validate causal links over time or examine these dynamics across different sectors to determine whether sectoral nuances affect the mediating effect.

latest.title: Digital Service Ecosystem Development through Strategic Entrepreneurship and University-Industry Partnerships
latest.venue: International Journal of Cyber and IT Service Management
latest.abstract: The role of higher education institutions in fostering innovation ecosystems has become increasingly important in the context of global economic transformation. However, empirical studies examining the combined influence of strategic global entrepreneurship and university–industry partnerships on innovation ecosystem performance remain limited, particularly in emerging economies. This study aims to investigate the impact of Strategic Global Entrepreneurship and University–Industry Partnerships on Innovation Ecosystem Performance in Indonesian higher education institutions. A quantitative approach was employed using a cross-sectional survey design, with data collected from 182 respondents, including lecturers, innovation managers, startup founders, and industry partners. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that both Strategic Global Entrepreneurship and University-Industry Partnerships have a positive and significant effect on Innovation Ecosystem Performance. Notably, university–industry partnerships demonstrate a stronger influence, highlighting the importance of collaborative mechanisms in driving innovation outcomes. This study contributes to the literature by integrating both constructs into a unified empirical model and provides practical insights for universities and policymakers in strengthening innovation ecosystems in emerging economies.

latest.title: ANALISIS PERAN LITERASI KEUANGAN DALAM MEMODERASI PENGARUH GAYA HIDUP TERHADAP PERILAKU KONSUMTIF PENGGUNA SHOPEE PAYLATER (STUDI KASUS PADA MAHASISWA FAKULTAS EKONOMI UNIVERSITAS NIAS)
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The use of digital financial services, particularly Shopee PayLater, provides students with convenient transaction options but may also be associated with less controlled consumption patterns. Lifestyle and financial management skills are important aspects to examine in understanding consumer behavior in deferred payment services. This study aims to analyze the effect of lifestyle on consumptive behavior and examine the moderating role of financial literacy among students of the Faculty of Economics at Universitas Nias. This research employed a quantitative approach using primary and secondary data. The sample consisted of 225 respondents selected through purposive sampling, based on the criterion that they were students who used Shopee PayLater. The data were analyzed using linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with IBM SPSS Statistics. The results indicate that lifestyle has a positive and statistically significant effect on consumptive behavior, with a significance value of less than 0.001 and an adjusted R-squared of 44.4%. The moderation test yielded a t-value of 0.342 and a significance value of 0.732, indicating that the interaction between lifestyle and financial literacy was not statistically significant. These findings suggest that lifestyle is associated with consumptive behavior, but financial literacy has not been shown to moderate this relationship. The results may inform the development of financial education initiatives and encourage more prudent consumption decisions among university students. ABSTRAK Penggunaan layanan keuangan digital, khususnya Shopee PayLater, memberikan kemudahan transaksi bagi mahasiswa, tetapi juga berpotensi berkaitan dengan pola konsumsi yang kurang terkendali. latest.title: Measuring conscious capitalism practices: development and validation of a scale
latest.abstract: Abstract Conscious Capitalism (CC) has gained prominence as a management approach rooted in ethical values, sustainability, and the creation of value for multiple stakeholders. Despite conceptual advancements, no validated scale currently exists to measure CC organizational practices. This study aimed to develop and validate the Conscious Capitalism Practices Scale (CCPS), grounded in established theoretical dimensions. Conducted in Brazil, the quantitative research involved two survey-based phases: a preliminary study ( n = 144) and a validation phase ( n = 391). Convergent, discriminant, and criterion validity were assessed through Confirmatory Factor Analysis and Structural Equation Modeling using SmartPLS 4 (version 4.0.9.2) and JASP (version 0.19.1). The final scale, comprising 10 factors and 43 items, demonstrated strong fit and reliability indices. The instrument contributes to the empirical operationalization of CC and offers a diagnostic tool for organizations committed to ethical and sustainable management practices.

latest.title: ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЯ УПРАВЛІННЯ ВИРОБНИЧИМИ ПРОЦЕСАМИ СІЛЬСЬКОГОСПОДАРСЬКИХ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ В УМОВАХ СУЧАСНИХ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЙ
latest.venue: Herald of Khmelnytskyi National University Economic sciences
latest.abstract: The article analyzes the relevance and essence of digitalizing production process management in agricultural enterprises, that is a topic of particular importance in the current business environment, especially taking into consideration martial law. It notes that the evolution and development of agricultural technologies necessitate managerial transformations, with digitalization serving as a key tool in this process. The article outlines the primary tools and capabilities associated with digitalizing the management of agricultural enterprises, citing examples such as cloud technologies, artificial intelligence, analytics platforms, the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain technology, precision farming systems, and digital accounting systems. Special attention is paid to blockchain technology, which is currently gaining traction and enhancing corporate transparency and efficiency by enabling process monitoring, data collection, execution of smart contracts, and fraud prevention. Blockchain technology plays a vital role in providing the information necessary for enterprise operations – a factor that is currently crucial for the effective management of modern agricultural businesses under the conditions of uncertainty and transformation. The study concludes that digitalizing production process management offers significant advantages to Ukrainian agricultural enterprises, bolstering their resilience and competitiveness. These benefits are realized through faster managerial decision-making supported by analytics tools and software, more efficient resource allocation in production, and the use of systems for monitoring and tracking logistics processes. All of this contributes to increased efficiency and labor productivity, improved product quality, responsiveness to changes

latest.title: Learning from sustainability pioneers: Drivers and barriers of sustainable manufacturing adoption in German industry
latest.abstract: Abstract Manufacturing companies face mounting pressure to adopt sustainable practices, yet a substantial gap persists between academic guidance and practical implementation. This study examines the perspective of pioneering manufacturers classified as innovators and early adopters of sustainable manufacturing (SM). This article seeks to answer the central question of how pioneers in the field successfully adopt SM measures and what implications arise for the wider industry. Building on a literature review of drivers and barriers, semi-structured expert interviews were conducted with ten sustainability and operations experts from eight German SM pioneers. Results reveal distinct barriers: bureaucratic delays, infrastructure deficits, and limited price premiums despite customer demand. They also highlight pioneer-specific drivers, including anticipation of future regulatory requirements and know-how accumulation through early innovation, which extend the current literature. Applying the diffusion-of-innovation framework, these findings explain the persistent adoption gap through unclear relative advantage, insufficient organizational compatibility, high complexity, and inadequate communication of outcomes. The twin transition shows potential synergies, whereby digital monitoring increases process transparency and supports the targeted implementation of sustainability measures. Decision makers are therefore encouraged to take indirect benefits into consideration, adopt digital monitoring systems, establish dedicated sustainability units, and nurture a transformation-supportive culture, thereby securing long-term competitiveness.

latest.title: How Financial Anxiety Shapes Affective Commitment: A Mediation Model of Self-Efficacy
latest.abstract: This paper will look at how financial anxiety relates to affective commitment in the employees of the public sector and how self-efficacy mediates the relationship between the two. The study is based on organizational behavior and social cognitive theory, according to which it is suggested that financial anxiety deprives employees of both direct and indirect emotional commitment to their organizations due to low self-efficacy. Validated self-report scales were used to collect data on 290 administrative workers working at a public university. The proposed model was tested using descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis and regression-based mediation analysis with bootstrapping (5,000 resamples). The results show that both self-efficacy and affective commitment are negatively correlated with financial anxiety, and that the self-efficacy is positively correlated with the affective commitment. The mediation analysis showed that self-efficacy partially mediates the correlation between financial anxiety and affective commitment. That is, financial anxiety deteriorates the emotional attachment of employees to their organization both directly and indirectly through undermining their confidence in their coping skills. The findings make contributions to the literature by incorporating the financial psychology and the organizational behavioral views and by emphasizing the contribution of personal psychology resources to organizational attitudes during economic stress. The research also has practical implications on the public sector organizations whereby the research indicates that interventions that target improvement in the self-efficacy and financial coping ability of the employees can be used to maintain affective commitment during economic uncertainty.

latest.title: Digital transformation and customer loyalty: The mediating role of co-created service experience in Indonesian banking
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractBanks invest in digital platforms expecting stronger loyalty. Yet, it remains unclear why some investments build durable relationships while others do not, because prior research conflates what customers do with how they experience it. This study tests whether co-created service experience mediates the relationship between customer-perceived digital transformation and customer loyalty among digital banking customers in Indonesia. Survey data were collected in 2025 from 360 customers of five banks in Medan, Indonesia, who had used mobile or internet banking for at least six months, ensuring direct experience with digital banking, and were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping. All four hypotheses were supported: digital transformation was strongly associated with co-created service experience (β = 0.659, p < 0.001) and significantly associated with loyalty directly (β = 0.425, p < 0.001); co-created service experience was significantly associated with loyalty (β = 0.478, p < 0.001) and partially mediated the digital transformation–loyalty relationship (indirect effect β = 0.315, p < 0.001; VAF = 42.6%), with the model explaining 67.8% of the variance in loyalty. Digital transformation is thus associated with loyalty through two distinct routes, only one of which depends on customers feeling like genuine participants. Institutional trust was not measured directly in this study, so the link between this pattern and Indonesia's institutional trust conditions is interpretive and requires further testing. Because the sample is limited to a single city, findings apply to this market and should not be generalized to Indonesian banking as a whole.

latest.title: ECONOMIC INVERSION IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: IMPLICIT INTANGIBLE ASSETS AND THE TRANSFORMATION OF CORPORATE VALUE
latest.abstract: The economic nature of implicit intangible assets is examined, and the concept of economic inversion of value is substantiated as a manifestation of the transformation of the sources of corporate value creation in the digital economy. Current trends in changes in the structure of companies’ market value and the sectoral distribution of intangible assets are analysed. Contradictions arising between classical financial theories and contemporary business valuation practices are identified. The economic essence of implicit intangible assets is revealed, and their role in the formation of competitive advantages and the growth of companies’ market value is determined. The author’s definitions of the concepts of "economic inversion of value" and "implicit intangible assets" are proposed. A conceptual model is developed to illustrate the interrelationship between the digitalisation of the economy, the increasing dominance of intangible capital, and the need to transform approaches to accounting and business valuation.

latest.title: Digital transformation in human resources: a case study of five-star hotels
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines the role of digital technologies in human resource (HR) operations and their impact on competitiveness and reputation in five-star hotels. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed, involving purposively selected 41 human resource managers from five-star hotels. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and analyzed in MAXQDA using a hybrid thematic analysis approach. Findings Digital HR practices act as strategic assets in dynamic capabilities (DC). While identifying significant benefits in recruitment efficiency, employee orientation, and organizational communication, it highlights critical emerging challenges such as “human touch anxiety” and “trust and privacy dilemmas”. These findings suggest that the hospitality industry's digital transformation requires a delicate balance between technological integration and its inherent human-centric nature. Practical implications The study provides strategic recommendations for hotel executives, emphasizing the need to establish digital ethics protocols and adopt an “HR marketing” approach. These strategies help optimize digital HR tools while maintaining employee loyalty and service quality in competitive markets. Originality/value The study offers rare qualitative evidence from a major developing tourism economy, filling a significant gap in a field often dominated by quantitative research from developed markets. By integrating the technology acceptance model (TAM), diffusion of innovations theory (DOI), the resource-based view (RBV), and the DC perspective, digital HR is positioned as a core strategic capability that generates sustainable competitive advantage in hospitality organizations.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: A Study on the Value Creation Pathways of Management Accounting in the Context of Digital Transformation: A Case Study of Midea Group
latest.abstract: Within the background of the digital economy, digital transformation has driven the accounting function to extend from traditional external financial disclosure to internal operational decision-making, making management accounting a pivotal tool for manufacturing enterprises to achieve value creation. The home appliance industry is highly competitive, with significant pressure on cost and inventory control; the effectiveness of digital management accounting practices directly impacts the operational quality of home appliance enterprises. This research selects Midea Group, a digital benchmark in the home appliance industry, for case analysis. With the theory of technology empowerment, drawing on core literature on digital management accounting and combining the TOE framework, this paper examines Midea Group’s implementation path for management accounting tools during its digital transformation, analyzes the effectiveness of these implementations and existing shortcomings, and proposes optimization recommendations based on these findings. Meanwhile, this paper aims to provide practical guidance for domestic manufacturing enterprises of a similar nature in implementing digital management accounting. It also contributes to the body of case study evidence on digital management accounting in the home appliance industry.

latest.title: Ethical change, legal normativity and social legitimacy
latest.abstract: This article examines organizational change in enterprises as a socio-legal process rather than a purely technical or managerial transformation. Drawing on the sociology of law and business ethics, it explores how legal norms, ethical expectations and institutional pressures shape the legitimacy of organizational change. The analysis adopts an interdisciplinary theoretical approach, engaging with the work of Luhmann, Bourdieu, Cotterrell, Habermas and institutional theory. Enterprises are conceptualized as social actors embedded in broader legal, cultural and normative environments, where ethical discourse functions both as a mechanism of control and a source of legitimacy. The article argues that organizational change involves processes of moral and legal legitimation through which enterprises negotiate social acceptance and institutional continuity. By framing organizational transformation as a socio-legal phenomenon, it contributes to law and society scholarship by demonstrating how legal structures and ethical norms jointly shape the conditions under which organizational change becomes legitimate, socially intelligible and sustainable.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Emotional and behavioral asymmetries in user responses to virtual versus human influencers
latest.abstract: As AI virtual influencers (AIVIs) proliferate, understanding human-AI emotional engagement is vital for advancing affective computing. To examine whether AIVIs evoke comparable affective responses to human influencers (HIs), we analyzed 156,918 Instagram comments that received 12+ million likes, integratinglarge language model (LLM)-derived knowledge graphs, emotion analysis, and machine learning. HI-directed discourse shows more differentiated emotional expression and a pattern consistent with more cohesive semantic networks than AIVI-directed discourse. AIVI-directed comments are less likely to express positive affect (24.8% vs. 41.5%) and also less likely to express negative affect (5.8% vs. 9.3%), indicating reduced affective expression of either valence rather than heightened negativity. This group-level tendency is not uniform: affective engagement varies substantially across AIVIs, and that variation is more closely associated with positive than with negative expression. Our Multi-Signal Embedding Network (MSEN), incorporating behavioral metrics and OpenAI semantic embeddings, classified influencer types from behavioral, affective and semantic features (F1 = 0.89), outperforming baselines including a state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM. These findings identify a boundary condition for the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm: human-like appearance can elicit social responses without producing affective and semantic response patterns as rich as those elicited by HIs.

latest.title: Examining Digital Human Resource Practices in Karachi, Pakistan: The Influence of Technological Change, Employee Attitude, and Employee Competency
latest.venue: International Journal of Business Strategy and Innovation
latest.abstract: This study examines the influence of Technological Change (TC) on Digital Human Resource Practices (DHRP), focusing on the roles of Employee Attitude (EA) and Employee Competency (EC) in Karachi, Pakistan. Data were collected from 244 respondents and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS 4. The findings reveal that Technological Change significantly and positively influences DHRP and Employee Attitude, while Employee Attitude significantly enhances DHRP. Employee Competency significantly moderates the relationship between Employee Attitude and DHRP, but the negative interaction effect does not support the hypothesized positive moderation. The study provides implications for digital HR implementation and future research.
