hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Hotel certifications are not only crucial for environmental sustainability, but also serve as

hot.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 30 loci associated with obsessive–compulsive disorder
hot.abstract: Abstract Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) affects ∼1% of children and adults and is partly caused by genetic factors. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis combining 53,660 OCD cases and 2,044,417 controls and identified 30 independent genome-wide significant loci. Gene-based approaches identified 249 potential effector genes for OCD, with 25 of these classified as the most likely causal candidates, including WDR6, DALRD3, CTNND1 and multiple genes in the MHC region. We estimated that ∼11,500 genetic variants explained 90% of OCD genetic heritability. OCD genetic risk was associated with excitatory neurons in the hippocampus and cortex, along with D1- and D2-type dopamine receptor-containing medium spiny neurons. OCD genetic risk was shared with 65 of 112 additional phenotypes, including all of the psychiatric disorders we examined. In particular, OCD shared genetic risk with anxiety, depression, anorexia nervosa, and Tourette syndrome, and was negatively associated with inflammatory bowel diseases, educational attainment, and body mass index.

hot.title: Digital Leadership and Sustainable Development: Enhancing Firm Sustainability Through Green Innovation and Top Management Innovativeness
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the crucial role of digital leadership in advancing sustainable development by fostering green innovation and enhancing firm sustainability. Building on Organizational Learning Theory (OLT) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory (DCT), this research fills a key gap by examining how digital leadership integrates digitalization with sustainable development, particularly within the Chinese information technology sector. The study investigates the impact of digital leadership on green innovation and sustainable performance, moderated by top management innovativeness. To enhance analytical robustness and minimize bias, a three‐phase time‐lagged data collection approach was employed to mitigate common method bias and ensure robust analysis, with responses from 413 employees representing diverse roles. The results indicate that digital leadership positively influences the green innovation process, which partially mediates the relationship between digital leadership and firm sustainability. Furthermore, the findings reveal that top management innovativeness amplifies the positive effects of digital leadership on green innovation, reinforcing the importance of leadership‐driven sustainability strategies. These insights contribute to the expanding discourse on corporate digital sustainability, demonstrating that digital transformation not only enhances operational efficiency but also serves as a catalyst for long‐term sustainable development. The study offers valuable implications for policymakers, business leaders, and researchers committed to leveraging digital leadership for corporate sustainability and the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

latest.title: Operational strategies for managing purchase decisions in festival shopping: Analyzing the role of fear of missing out (FOMO) in the digital transformation era
latest.venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
latest.abstract: Purpose: For most consumers who experience fear of missing out, regret related to falling behind trends outweighs regret related to financial costs. In fact, the intensity of the attraction created through fear of missing out is positively correlated with impulse buying, which potentially reduces self-control during shopping activities. Hence, fear of missing out is considered a psychological disorder that affects the mental health of the individual. Therefore, this study aims to explain the reactive-behavioral outcomes (e.g., impulsive buying decisions) by emphasizing the perceptual drivers of the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) phenomenon within the context of festival shopping opportunities in the digital transformation era.Methodology: This study is a basic-applied research based on its purpose and a mixed research based on its research strategy. The qualitative strategy used in the first stage of the research is grounded theory and the quantitative strategies used in this survey-correlational research. The qualitative participants included marketing and sales consultants as well as professors of business, marketing, and e-commerce, 10 of whom were selected as participants through non-probability judgmental sampling. The statistical population of the quantitative part of the study is people who visited various festivals and made various purchases.The sampling method in the quantitative section was random, and the sample size was determined to be 221 participants based on relationship of Cohen. To prevent sample attrition, about 240 questionnaires were distributed in this study and 229 questionnaires were returned to the researcher.Findings: The results showed that perceptual drivers (positive customer perception of the brand, deceptive advertising, customer experience,

latest.title: Towards a Conceptual Integration of Masstige in Consumer Behaviour through a Kaleidoscopic View
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract: The purpose of this research paper is to conduct a comprehensive scoping review with the objective to examine the advancement of masstige marketing as an essential notion in consumer-brand engagement researches. The study covers a multitude of facets of masstige marketing literature, comprising frameworks, methodologies, antecedents, outcomes, mediators, moderators through the examination of 88 studies. In an effort to incorporate masstige marketing notion within the consumer-brand engagement research, this paper highlights the necessity of constructing robust frameworks and tackling the quantitative difficulties. This scoping review provides insights to practitioners and academics who desire to further explore the domain of masstige. Keywords: Brand Management, Masstige, Luxury, Consumer-Brand Relationship, Prestige Brands

latest.title: Pleasure or annoyance? The opposing effects of food-service rituals
latest.venue: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management
latest.abstract: Purpose Food-service rituals are increasingly prevalent in hospitality practice, yet their effects in real-world settings remain underexplored. Drawing on Interaction Ritual Chain theory, this research aims to investigate when and why food-service rituals enhance versus undermine encounter satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach Three video-based experiments were conducted in a restaurant setting. Findings Study 1 shows a positive main effect of food-service rituals on encounter satisfaction. Study 2 demonstrates that food-service rituals enhance satisfaction by evoking pleasure among customers with hedonic consumption goals but elicit annoyance among customers with utilitarian goals. Study 3 further reveals that food-service rituals exert a positive effect under communal customer-brand relationship norms, but backfire under exchange relationship norms. Practical implications This study offers valuable guidance for restaurant operators. Businesses should consider customers’ consumption goals and customer-brand relationship norms when implementing food-service rituals. Originality/value This study enriches the hospitality management literature by developing a more balanced understanding of food-service rituals and highlighting the conditions and emotional mechanisms that shape customer reactions.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: From “mine” to “me”: how perceived NFT attributes shape brand resonance in Chinese Generation Z sports fandom
latest.venue: International Journal of Sports Marketing and Sponsorship
latest.abstract: Purpose Situated within sports fandom and China’s regulated digital asset environment, this study examines how perceived uniqueness, scarcity, controllability, and non-fungible tokens (NFT) symbolism shape brand resonance through psychological ownership and customer-brand identification among Generation Z fans. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on psychological ownership theory and social identity theory, the study tests a serial mediation model using survey data from 489 Chinese Generation Z sports fans and partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings Perceived uniqueness, controllability, and NFT symbolism strengthen psychological ownership, which increases customer-brand identification and, in turn, brand resonance. This pattern supports a layered process from perceived NFT attributes to ownership, identification, and sustained fan-brand relationships. Perceived scarcity has no significant direct or indirect effects. Research limitations/implications Psychological ownership explains how NFTs become personally meaningful, while customer-brand identification links ownership to loyalty, attachment, community, and engagement. Sports brands operating in regulated digital markets should provide meaningful opportunities for fans to express their affiliation, exercise control, and participate in brand communities, rather than relying primarily on scarcity. Originality/value This study integrates ownership and identity perspectives to explain how sport brand NFTs foster digital belonging and brand resonance in sports fandom. It also provides evidence from China, where NFT circulation and speculative activities operate under regulatory constraints.

latest.title: Digital transformation and customer loyalty: The mediating role of co-created service experience in Indonesian banking
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractBanks invest in digital platforms expecting stronger loyalty. Yet, it remains unclear why some investments build durable relationships while others do not, because prior research conflates what customers do with how they experience it. This study tests whether co-created service experience mediates the relationship between customer-perceived digital transformation and customer loyalty among digital banking customers in Indonesia. Survey data were collected in 2025 from 360 customers of five banks in Medan, Indonesia, who had used mobile or internet banking for at least six months, ensuring direct experience with digital banking, and were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping. All four hypotheses were supported: digital transformation was strongly associated with co-created service experience (β = 0.659, p < 0.001) and significantly associated with loyalty directly (β = 0.425, p < 0.001); co-created service experience was significantly associated with loyalty (β = 0.478, p < 0.001) and partially mediated the digital transformation–loyalty relationship (indirect effect β = 0.315, p < 0.001; VAF = 42.6%), with the model explaining 67.8% of the variance in loyalty. Digital transformation is thus associated with loyalty through two distinct routes, only one of which depends on customers feeling like genuine participants. Institutional trust was not measured directly in this study, so the link between this pattern and Indonesia's institutional trust conditions is interpretive and requires further testing. Because the sample is limited to a single city, findings apply to this market and should not be generalized to Indonesian banking as a whole.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Effect of past relationship quality on brand hate: a serial mediation effect of perceived betrayal and blame attribution
latest.venue: The Journal of Marketing Theory and Practice
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine how past relationship quality with a brand can influence the development of brand hate and its outcomes. Drawing on an appraisal-based perspective, the study examines perceived betrayal as an affective response to violated relational expectations and blame attribution as a subsequent cognitive evaluation through which previously positive consumer–brand relationships can escalate into brand hate. Using the hierarchical brand hate dimensions, a serial mediation model is proposed between past relationship quality and hot, cool, and cold brand hate, through perceived betrayal and blame attribution. A cross-sectional survey was conducted to collect data from N = 560 Indian consumers. The model was tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that the effect of past relationship quality on the three brand hate dimensions is serially mediated by perceived betrayal and blame attribution. Hot brand hate affects consumers’ engagement in negative e-Word-of-Mouth (eWOM), cool and cold brand hate lead to reduced patronage, but only cold brand hate predicts brand avoidance. This study integrates affective and cognitive processes within an appraisal-based framework and empirically validates the hierarchical structure of brand hate. The findings provide support for the “love-becomes-hate” effect and highlight the importance for brands of recognizing customers with strong past relationships and proactively mitigating perceptions of betrayal.

latest.title: An Empirical Analysis of Factors Influencing Brand Equity in Coffee Shops: A Study of Jakarta, Indonesia
latest.venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in Jakarta is a direct consequence of Indonesia’s strong contribution to global coffee production as the world’s fourth-largest coffee producer. The number of coffee shops in Indonesia has reached 10,000 outlets. Due to increased competition among coffee shops, businesses are offering better service quality, innovative products, and improved ambiance and atmosphere to enhance brand loyalty, which eventually contributes to brand equity. However, limited studies have investigated the brand equity factors of coffee shop brands in Jakarta, despite the intense market competition among them. This study investigates how various brand-related factors, such as brand awareness, perceived quality, brand association, and brand loyalty, influence the overall brand equity of coffee shop brands in this highly competitive market. This study adopted a descriptive, explorative, and cross-sectional design with quantitative methods to analyze data collected from a representative sample of coffee shop consumers in Jakarta. Data were collected from 390 respondents from Jakarta city of Indonesia from 390 respondents from Jakarta, Indonesia, and were analyzed using SmartPLS. The statistical analysis confirms that there is a significant relationship between the four factors and brand equity, with perceived quality being the most influential factor among the study variables. This study provides strategic managerial recommendations for coffee shop businesses in Jakarta to enhance brand equity, underscoring the vital role of superior perceived quality while supporting sustainable business growth.

latest.title: From sole to soul: modes of meaning-making in contemporary sneaker collecting
latest.abstract: How does collecting remain meaningful in a relatively sterile, transparent marketplace driven by disenchanted financial logic and seamless, frictionless consumption options? This study explores how sneaker collectors sustain and create new meanings for contemporary sneaker collecting in response to the convenience and saturation of online (re)sell marketplaces. Drawing on in-depth interviews with Dutch sneaker collectors (n = 20), we identify five collector orientations based on the strategies they employ to make the practice meaningful: (1) expressionists, (2) social connectors, (3) aesthetes, (4) completionists, and (5) hunters. Each represents a different mode of engagement with sneaker collecting, whether through identity work, aesthetic appreciation, or strategic navigation of market dynamics. Expressionists use sneakers to construct biographical narratives, while social connectors prioritize shared belonging and community. Aesthetes are guided by aesthetic and cultural value, and completionists and hunters create meaning either by achieving closure or constantly extending the thrill of the hunt. These findings suggest that contemporary collecting cannot be reduced to ‘shallow’ consumerism, nor can it be understood as an individual and isolated practice. Instead, collecting acquires meaning through the interplay between producers, consumers, and the digital and physical spaces in which it takes place.

latest.title: Socio Technical Drivers of Impulse Buying in Live Streaming Fashionpreneurship
latest.abstract: This study addresses the rapid growth of live-streaming commerce in Indonesia and its impact on impulse buying behavior within emerging digital economies. Integrating the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework with Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory, this research aims to examine how socio technical stimuli streamer factors, platform affordances, and perceived brand value, influence consumers’ emotional (shopping happiness) and cognitive (ongoing trust) states, which subsequently drive impulse buying. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data from 300 consumers who purchased local fashion products via Shopee Live and TikTok Shop. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess measurement validity and structural relationships. The results indicate that all hypothesized relationships are statistically significant. Socio-technical stimuli significantly influence both shopping happiness and ongoing trust, which in turn positively affect impulse buying, with shopping happiness emerging as the strongest predictor. This study contributes by offering an integrated socio-technical perspective on consumer behavior in live commerce and provides practical implications for enhancing engagement and trust. It also supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 8 and SDG 9, by promoting sustainable digital commerce and empowering local fashion businesses through technology-driven innovation.

latest.title: Party Failure, Voter Emotions and Retaliation Intentions in the Context of Digitalization
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping the value relationship that political parties, like firms, maintain with their stakeholders; voters’ reactions are now visible not only at the ballot box but also on social media and in interpersonal networks. This study adapts concepts from the consumer-brand relationship and consumer retaliation literature to political parties and examines the effect of perceived party failure severity on three response intentions (direct complaining to the party, public complaining on social media and negative word of mouth) through voters’ anger and perceived betrayal. The effects of perceived justice and inferred benevolence on negative emotions and the moderating roles of party love and party trust are also tested. Data from 383 eligible voters in Türkiye, collected through an online survey, were analysed using confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modelling, bootstrapping and moderation analyses. Failure severity strongly increases anger and perceived betrayal, which are linked to different response channels: anger to direct complaining, which functions as voice directed at the party, and betrayal to public complaining on social media and negative word of mouth. At the level of total indirect effects, however, failure severity increases only direct complaining; its total indirect effect on social media is non-significant and that on negative word of mouth is negative, so failure translates into indirect retaliation only to the extent that it is experienced as betrayal. Hypotheses regarding perceived justice, inferred benevolence, party love and party trust were not supported. Interpreted through a value co-destruction lens, the findings contribute to the political marketing literature on the dark side of the voter-party relationship
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Employee Brand Equity and Decent Work in Chinese Hospitality
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Drawing on extended‐self theory, this study examines how employee brand equity relates to decent work in Chinese branded hospitality organizations. Data were collected from 440 employees across 25 branded hospitality organizations in Hainan, China. The results indicate that brand endorsement, brand allegiance, and brand consistent behavior each have significant positive direct effects on decent work, as well as indirect effects through brand psychological ownership. Brand psychological ownership partially mediates these relationships, while perceived brand value fit positively moderates the relationship between brand psychological ownership and decent work. These findings extend employee brand equity research by identifying decent work as an employee‐centered outcome and by clarifying the mediating role of brand psychological ownership and the boundary role of perceived brand value fit. The study also offers practical insights into how branded hospitality organizations may support more positive employee work experiences.

latest.title: Transforming cultural heritage into modern marketing narratives: A thematic analysis of HEPA Coffee’s brand archetypes through a Gen Z perspective
latest.abstract: Makale Türü: Araştırma makalesiBu çalışma, HEPA Coffee'nin Puduhepa figürü üzerinden inşa ettiği marka kimliğini ve bu anlatının Z kuşağı tarafından nasıl algılandığını incelemektedir.Nitel araştırma tasarımında marka kurucusuyla derinlemesine mülakat ve Z kuşağı katılımcılarıyla odak grup görüşmeleri gerçekleştirilmiştir. Bulgular, markanın stratejik olarak Hükümdar ve Kahraman arketipleri etrafında kurgulandığını ve Puduhepa figürünün güçlü bir anlatı unsuru olarak işlev gördüğünü ortaya koymaktadır.Bununla birlikte, Z kuşağı açısından doğallık (Masum arketipi) artık temel bir beklenti düzeyine karşılık gelirken; daha gizemli ve sembolik (Sihirbaz arketipi) bir görsel dil talep edilmektedir.Araştırma, kültürel sermayenin etkili bir marka deneyimine dönüşebilmesi için görsel anlatı tutarlılığı ile dijital mikroanlatıların kritik bir rol oynadığını göstermektedir.

latest.title: Relationship Quality toward Sufficiency Economy-Aligned Sustainable Brands: Evidence from Thailands Generation Z
latest.abstract: Purpose: This research aims to capture the dimensions of consumer-brand relationship quality between young adult Gen Z consumers and Sufficiency Economy Philosophy (SEP)-aligned sustainable brands by applying the Investment Model. While previous studies have primarily examined individual dimensions of sustainable brand relationship quality, this study integrated multiple motivational dimensions of brand relationship quality within the Investment Model for SEP-aligned sustainable brands. Research design, data and methodology: A mixed-method approach was employed, beginning with qualitative exploration followed by quantitative research. Data were collected through an online questionnaire survey, yielding 277 usable responses, predominantly from university students, representing young adult Gen Z consumers in Thailand. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was conducted to test a second-order reflective measurement model of brand relationship quality. Results: The results indicate that the Gen Z consumers perceive SEP alignment as an integral aspect of sustainable corporate brands. Brand relationship quality in this context is a multidimensional construct comprising economic satisfaction, trust, pride, self-connection, all of which demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity, with trust as the strongest reflection (β = 0.870), followed by pride (β = 0.783). Major Findings: Trust emerged as the strongest reflective construct, followed by pride, economic satisfaction, and self-connection, highlighting the importance of SEP-aligned sustainable branding.

latest.title: Cultural Identity and Sustainability in Airline Service Quality: Thai Airways Case Study
latest.abstract: This study examines how cultural identity and environmental sustainability can be integrated into airline service quality in the specific context of Thai Airways. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered to international passengers who had flown with the airline within the previous six months; 596 usable questionnaires were obtained from 650 distributed at Suvarnabhumi Airport between January and March 2024. The instrument combined SERVQUAL, sustainability perception, cultural service value, satisfaction, loyalty, and travel-characteristic measures. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were used as the principal analytical procedures. The model showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.962, TLI = 0.958, RMSEA = 0.044, SRMR = 0.038), while scale reliability ranged from 0.78 to 0.94. Service expectations were associated with satisfaction both directly and indirectly through service quality, with a reported total effect of 0.610. Behavioral patterns also showed significant relationships with satisfaction, and visible environmental initiatives were the strongest sustainability-related predictor of service perceptions. The findings indicate that service quality in a national carrier is best understood as an integrated configuration of core service performance, culturally distinctive delivery, and credible sustainability practices rather than as independent service attributes. This integrated perspective provides the empirical basis for the proposed SSQ framework.

latest.title: Brand forgiveness: a scoping review and agenda for future research
latest.abstract: Purpose Brand forgiveness reflects consumers’ willingness to maintain or restore relationships with brands following service failures, ethical controversies and marketplace transgressions. The purpose of this study is to conduct a scoping review of the theoretical development, conceptual foundations and future directions of brand forgiveness research. Design/methodology/approach The review synthesizes 80 studies published between 2009 and 2025 using scoping review guidelines and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analyses reporting procedures. The analysis examines theoretical foundations, methodological approaches, antecedents, mediators, moderators and outcomes. Findings Brand forgiveness literature is grounded in coping, attribution and justice-based theories of post-transgression evaluation, while relational and identity-based processes remain less developed. The literature identifies firm-, consumer- and brand/communication-related antecedents, along with cognitive, emotional and social mechanisms shaping forgiveness. Methodologically, the field relies largely on experiments and cross-sectional surveys, limiting understanding of forgiveness as a dynamic process. Research limitations/implications The review identifies theoretical, methodological and contextual gaps and proposes directions for advancing brand forgiveness research. Originality/value This review synthesizes fragmented brand forgiveness research and conceptualizes forgiveness as a process involving cognitive interpretation, emotional regulation, moral evaluation and relationship repair.

latest.title: Examining The Relationships Between The Need For Social Approval And Sustainable Consumption Behavior
latest.venue: Türkiye Mesleki ve Sosyal Bilimler Dergisi
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the relationships between individuals’ need for social approval and sustainable consumption behaviors. Accordingly, the need for social approval is conceptualized in terms of three dimensions—sensitivity to others’ judgments, social withdrawal, and leaving a good impression—and the relationships between these dimensions and four dimensions of sustainable consumption behavior, namely environmental sensitivity, reusability, saving, and unneeded consumption, are examined. Within the scope of the study, data were collected through an online survey from 393 university students with different levels of educational attainment who were selected using a convenience sampling method. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analyses, and multiple regression analyses. The findings indicate that social motivations may be associated with sustainable consumption behaviors and that the nature of these relationships may vary across the dimensions of the need for social approval. The findings further suggest that social approval may serve as a functional mechanism for promoting sustainable consumption. Accordingly, the study offers implications for businesses and policymakers regarding the use of social norms to encourage more sustainable consumption practices.

latest.title: Identidade em cena: cultura pop, pertencimento e decisões de compra
latest.venue: Contextus - Revista Contemporânea de Economia e Gestão
latest.abstract: Contextualização: As decisões de compra de itens vinculados à cultura POP frequentemente ultrapassam a lógica estritamente funcional, sendo orientadas por significados simbólicos, identificação com universos narrativos e vínculos afetivos. Objetivo: Esta pesquisa investigou de que modo o uso das redes sociais (URS), a nostalgia (NOST), a formação de comunidade (FC) e o vínculo com a cultura POP (VCP) influenciam o comportamento de compra (CC). Método: Os dados foram coletados por questionário online entre os meses de setembro e dezembro de 2024. A amostra foi composta por 388 respondentes válidos. Para a análise, optou-se pela Modelagem de Equações Estruturais via Mínimos Quadrados Parciais (PLS-SEM), tendo como ferramenta de apoio o software SmartPLS4. Resultados: Os resultados indicaram que o uso das redes sociais influencia positivamente a formação de comunidade e, principalmente, o vínculo com a cultura POP, enquanto o vínculo com a cultura POP se destacou como o preditor mais forte do comportamento de compra. Adicionalmente, verificou-se que o uso das redes sociais influencia o comportamento de compra tanto de forma direta quanto indiretamente por meio do vínculo com a cultura POP, ao passo que a nostalgia apresentou influência direta de menor magnitude e não sustentou efeitos indiretos via formação de comunidade ou vínculo com a cultura POP. Conclusões: Os achados reforçam a centralidade do vínculo com a cultura POP como mecanismo explicativo do consumo em ambientes digitais, ao evidenciar que o uso das redes sociais contribui para a compra principalmente quando fortalece a identificação simbólica com esse universo.

latest.title: Pazarlama İletişiminde Teknolojik Nostaljinin Yeniden İnşası: Ülker Albeni ‘Ajda Pekkan’ Reklamı Üzerine Hiper-Gerçeklik ve Restoratif Nostalji Eksenli Bir İnceleme
latest.abstract: Bu çalışma, Ülker Albeni’nin Ajda Pekkan temalı reklamını teknolojik nostaljinin pazarlama iletişimindeki inşası bağlamında, Svetlana Boym’un restoratif nostalji ve Jean Baudrillard’ın hiper-gerçeklik kuramları ekseninde analiz etmektedir. Kuramsal düzlemde restoratif nostalji, geçmişin doğrusal gerçekliğini ve zamanın getirdiği tahribatı yapay zekâ gibi araçlarla ‘telafi edilmesi gereken bir boşluk’ olarak görürken; bu süreç Baudrillardcı perspektifte gerçeğin yerini alan ve orijinalinden daha ‘otantik’ algılanan hiper-gerçek bir simülasyon üretmektedir. Roland Barthes’ın göstergebilimsel yöntemiyle yapılan çözümlemede; Ajda Pekkan’ın 1990, 2000 ve 2025 yıllarını temsil eden figürleri ile ürünün çikolata, karamel ve bisküvi katmanları arasında kurulan ritmik uyumun, tüketici belleğinde ‘değişmeyen öz’ mitini yapılandırdığı saptanmıştır. Yapay zekâ destekli gençleştirme (de-aging) teknolojisinin Ajda Pekkan’ın kültürel ikonluğuyla birleşmesi, sanatsal bir ‘aura’nın sentetik olarak yeniden üretilmesine ve markanın zamanın aşındırıcı etkisinden arındırılmış, zamansız bir otorite olarak mühürlenmesine olanak tanımıştır.

latest.title: IMPACT OF PRICE SENSITIVITY ON CONSUMERS’ DECISION-MAKING IN AIRLINE TICKET PURCHASES
latest.venue: Journal of Global Peace-Marketing and Communications (JGPMC)
latest.abstract: This research examines how price sensitivity shapes consumers’ decisions when purchasing airline tickets in Calabar, Cross River State. Its specific focus is on the role of alternative evaluation and sensitivity to booking time. Two null hypotheses were tested: that neither alternative evaluation nor booking-time sensitivity significantly influences ticket-purchase decisions. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, covering passengers travelling to different destinations through Margaret Ekpo International Airport. Stratified sampling was used to allocate the 400 respondents among Ibom Air, Cally Air and Air Peace. Primary data were obtained with a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, means and standard deviations) and multiple linear regression. The findings show that respondents placed the greatest emphasis on promotional deals and discounts when comparing fares (mean = 4.58), while booking early to obtain cheaper tickets was the highest-rated booking-time behaviour (mean = 3.74). Regression results indicate statistically significant effects for alternative evaluation (p = 0.004) and booking-time sensitivity (p = 0.002), both below the 0.05 threshold. The study concludes that comparing available options and choosing booking times carefully can influence ticket-purchase decisions. Airlines are therefore encouraged to review pricing arrangements and strengthen appropriate discount and promotional programmes to attract and retain customers. Keywords: Airline Ticket Purchases, Alternative Evaluation, Booking Time Sensitivity, Price Sensitivity, Consumers’ Decision-Making.

latest.title: Reconciling Fragmented Consumer Figures: The Metaconsumer as a Unifying Concept for Circularity
latest.abstract: This article argues that the transition toward a circular economy requires a more integrative understanding of individuals than the traditional consumer concept allows. While marketing and consumer behavior scholarship has developed several figures, including the green consumer, creative consumer, collaborative consumer, alternative consumer, working consumer, and prosumer, these concepts remain partial and insufficiently fluid to capture the multiple roles required by circular practices. Building on these antecedents, the paper advances the metaconsumer as a unifying concept for interpreting contemporary circularity through a practice-based framework. The metaconsumer is presented as a cross-cutting figure whose agency unfolds through five constitutive role families: redistribution, mutualization, citizen movements, self-production, and independent production. Descriptive evidence from a cross-sectional pan-Canadian survey (n = 1,019) indicates that all five role families, in both their self-directed and other-directed forms, can be observed in self-reported practice, with acquisition-type practices such as second-hand reuse far more common than production-type practices. The data cannot yet capture movement between roles, which the paper identifies as the construct’s distinctive claim and as the priority for further research. The paper concludes that the metaconsumer offers a theoretically grounded and empirically plausible lens for understanding the transition from linear consumption to circularity.

latest.title: The Impact of Apple's Advertising Marketing on People Between the Ages of 20 and 30
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: This report examines the impact of Apple's promotional activities on purchase intentions among consumers aged 20–30, focusing on four key areas: physical retail stores, the "Shot on iPhone" campaign, product launch events, and the brand narrative shift from Steve Jobs to Tim Cook. Using a mixed-method approach, the study collected 50 valid questionnaire responses and conducted five semi-structured interviews with young Apple users. Findings indicate that Apple's retail stores enhance brand trust through tangible evidence and atmosphere, yet only 34% of respondents rated the in-store experience as highly impressive. The "Shot on iPhone" campaign effectively communicates creativity and authenticity (60% awareness), but user participation remains low. Product launches generate global excitement and influence purchase decisions, though signs of "innovation fatigue" are evident among younger demographics. The evolution from a revolutionary to a more pragmatic brand narrative reflects Apple's adaptation to a mature smartphone market, but also risks diluting its distinctive appeal. Overall, Apple's value‑bundled marketing positively shapes brand identity and shopping willingness, yet strategic adjustments—such as fostering interactive communities, creating layered recognition for creators, and balancing innovation with practicality—are recommended to sustain engagement and counteract fatigue. This research provides empirical insights into how symbolic values influence consumer behaviour in the premium electronics sector.

latest.title: DECODIFICANDO O CONSUMO DE MODA DE SEGUNDA MÃO NO SUL GLOBAL: UMA TIPOLOGIA PSICOGRÁFICA A PARTIR DO RIO DE JANEIRO
authors: Renata Maria de Almeida Bastos Gomes
latest.abstract: Tomando o Rio de Janeiro, um dos principais polos difusores de tendências de cultura na América Latina, este artigo propõe uma tipologia psicográfica exploratória de consumidores de moda de segunda mão no Sul Global. Parte-se da premissa de que o crescimento desse mercado, embora parcialmente explicado por variáveis demográficas e motivações econômicas, carece de explicações com base nas dimensões simbólicas, identitárias, estéticas e éticas do consumo são. Com base em revisão da literatura sobre sociedade de consumo, consumo e identidade, economia circular e moda de segunda mão, e a partir de observação participante de uma das autoras e de entrevistas em profundidade com profissionais e especialistas do setor no Rio de Janeiro, foram construídos e discutidos cinco perfis de consumidores: econômico, garimpeiro, autoral, consciente e acidental. Os resultados indicam que esses perfis servem como lentes analíticas que se sobrepõem e se deslocam conforme o contexto de compra, o tipo de peça e o momento de vida do consumidor. O confronto sistemático entre os perfis identificados empiricamente e a literatura internacional revisada revela uma hierarquia de contribuição: três perfis replicam, em contexto latino-americano, construtos já validados internacionalmente; um perfil sintetiza conceitos até então dispersos na literatura; e um perfil – o acidental – não encontra equivalente direto na literatura revisada, configurando-se como a principal contribuição teórica do estudo. O artigo oferece implicações práticas para a gestão de brechós, bazares e plataformas digitais de revenda, com destaque para a importância do ponto de venda físico na captura do consumidor acidental.

latest.title: Beyond a Name: The CAPE Framework for Names, Nicknames, and (Nick)Naming in Marketing
AI-Personalised Marketing and Consumer Brand Loyalty: The Roles of Perceived Autonomy and Psychological Reactance
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has enabled firms to personalise marketing communications, recommendations, pricing, timing, and service interactions at the individual consumer level. While such personalisation can enhance relevance and strengthen consumer–brand relationships, it can also raise concerns about surveillance and manipulation, potentially threatening consumers’ perceived freedom of choice and triggering psychological reactance. This conceptual paper develops an autonomy–reactance framework to explain the conditions under which AI-personalised marketing strengthens or weakens consumer brand loyalty. Drawing on psychological reactance theory, selfdetermination theory, the personalisation–privacy paradox, and consumer–brand engagement research, the framework proposes that perceived personalisation quality strengthens brand loyalty by enhancing perceived relevance and engagement. In contrast, perceived intrusiveness may weaken loyalty by reducing perceived autonomy and increasing psychological reactance.

latest.title: Determinants of Consumer Loyalty toward Huawei Tablets: The Roles of Brand Image, Product Quality, and Consumer Satisfaction
latest.abstract: This study examines associations of brand image, product quality, and consumer satisfaction with consumer loyalty toward Huawei tablets in Indonesia. A purposive survey of 400 users was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Positive direct associations were found for brand image (β = 0.285; p = 0.027), product quality (β = 0.368; p = 0.018), and consumer satisfaction (β = 0.258; p = 0.036). The model explained 68.2% of loyalty variance (R² = 0.682). Product quality had the largest estimated coefficient. These findings concern surveyed users and do not establish causal effects or national representativeness.

latest.title: Banka Reklamlarına Duyulan Güvenin Banka Sadakatine Etkisinde Bankanın Kurumsal İmajının Rolü
latest.abstract: Bu araştırmanın amacı, banka reklamlarına duyulan güvenin banka sadakati üzerindeki etkisini ve bu ilişkide bankanın kurumsal imajının aracılık rolünü incelemektir. Günümüzde bankacılık sektöründe yoğun rekabet koşullarının artması, bankaların müşterileriyle güven temelli ve sürdürülebilir ilişkiler kurmasını önemli hâle getirmiş durumdadır. Bu süreçte reklam faaliyetleri, yalnızca bilgilendirme amaçlı değil, aynı zamanda bankaya yönelik güven ve olumlu kurumsal algı oluşturma açısından stratejik bir iletişim unsuru haline gelmiştir. Araştırmanın evrenini Türkiye’de yaşayan 18 yaş ve üzeri bireyler oluşturmakta olup, araştırma verileri çevrim içi anket yöntemiyle 487 katılımcıdan elde edilmiştir. Verilerin analizinde geçerlilik, güvenilirlik analizleri ve hipotezlerin test edilmedinde yapısal eşitlik modellemesi (YEM) kullanılmıştır. Araştırma sonuçları, kullanılan ölçeklerin geçerli ve güvenilir olduğunu göstermiştir.
