hot.title: Using Augmented Reality to Strengthen Consumer/Brand Relationships: The Case of Luxury Brands
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT Though augmented reality (AR) is increasingly adopted in marketing, its capacity to foster consumers' engagement and attachment remain tenuous, exposing an important literature‐based gap. Addressing this gap, we deploy social presence theory and luxury consumption theory to develop and test a model that proposes that consumers' engagement with AR‐deploying luxury brands drives the development of their perceived brand warmth, social value, and brand competence, in turn impacting their brand attachment. To explore these issues, we draw on survey data from a sample of 537 luxury apparel and automotive consumers. The results using structural equation modelling (SEM) show that first, luxury consumers who exhibit high engagement with the AR‐deploying brand perceive higher levels of brand warmth, ‐competence, and social value, in turn raising their attachment to the AR‐deploying luxury brand. Overall, the findings highlight AR's strategic capacity to engage consumers and raise the brand's perceived brand warmth, competence, and social value, in turn boosting individuals' attachment to the AR‐deploying brand.

hot.title: How Gamification Features Drive Brand Loyalty: The Mediating Roles of Consumer Experience and Brand Engagement
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: In the digital age, gamification has emerged as a paramount strategy for strengthening brand–consumer interaction. Despite the fact that existing studies have extensively probed further into its effects on brand communication and sales performance, rare investigations have been reported to throw light upon how gamification features influence consumer experience, brand engagement, and brand loyalty, as well as the potential mediating mechanisms involved. For this reason, this research delved into these correlations by employing structural equation modeling (SEM) grounded in 461 valid responses from consumers familiar with a co-branded gamification campaign between a tea beverage brand and a gaming IP. The results illustrated that immersion, achievement, and social interaction dramatically reinforced consumer experience, which led to brand engagement and, in turn, strengthened brand loyalty. Furthermore, consumer experience and brand engagement both mediated gamification feature effects on brand loyalty. By constructing and validating a generalized model, the current study not only practically expands the gamification literature but also empirically illuminates mechanisms through which gamification features contribute to loyalty formation in co-branded settings.

hot.title: Applying the S-O-R model to explore impulsive buying behavior driven by influencers on social commerce websites
hot.abstract: ., videos and articles). When fans encounter these messages, they may make unplanned purchases, resulting in impulse buying behavior, a long-standing issue in marketing research. This study aims to explore the factors that lead to such behavior. Using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) model as a framework, the study investigates how interactions between individuals and influencer content (Stimuli) trigger psychological changes in consumers, namely positive affect, flow state, and emotional attachment (Organism), which in turn lead to impulse buying behavior (Response). The study surveyed fans who had previously purchased products recommended by influencers, collecting 404 valid responses. The findings reveal that: (1) Consumers' psychological changes (positive affect, flow state, and emotional attachment) significantly and positively influence impulse buying behavior. (2) Scarcity, discounted price, review quality, and observational learning also have significant positive effects on impulse buying. (3) Social presence and sense of belonging significantly enhance flow state. (4) Entertainment and informativeness significantly enhance emotional attachment.

hot.title: Are Retail Consumers Willing to Pay for All Circular Products? A Study on Consumer Perception of the Circular Economy in Retail
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The planetary crisis, stemming from overconsumption and unsustainable production patterns, necessitates a shift towards balanced economic, environmental and social growth. The circular economy presents a promising solution by promoting material recirculation. While its success relies on collaboration among various stakeholders, consumers are crucial for accepting circular economy products and business models. However, despite increasing environmental awareness, the literature shows that many consumers resist purchasing previously used products due to perceived inferiority, risk and low quality, which could hinder the adoption of circular economy products. Understanding consumer behaviour, particularly their willingness to buy and pay for circular economy products, is essential for businesses seeking to promote sustainable consumption and achieve market growth. This study investigates consumer perceptions of circular economy, using simplified terms of reused, recycled and recovered, across 11 product categories through a quantitative survey of 607 Australian respondents. The results indicate that personal financial benefits are prioritised over ecological reasons, and there is variability in perceived product performance across categories. Additionally, price sensitivity and affordability play a key role in consumer decision‐making. Notably, while younger and male consumers show a greater inclination to purchase circular economy products, the broader consumer base remains unwilling to pay a premium. These insights can guide businesses and policymakers in developing targeted strategies emphasising price, functionality and quality to enhance consumer acceptance and adoption of circular economy products. We advance theory by demonstrating that consumer decisions ar

hot.title: Effects of financial consumer protection on brand love and brand advocacy
hot.abstract: Abstract Financial consumer protection has emerged as a critical global trend. This study examines how financial consumer protection affects brand advocacy in the context of retail banks in Hong Kong. Structural equation modelling was used to analyse a sample of 300 responses to an online survey. The results showed that fairness, transparency, and data privacy protection affected customer satisfaction, while governance had no significant effect on it. Customer satisfaction was positively associated with both brand love and brand advocacy. Brand love had a strong relationship with brand advocacy. Customer satisfaction also mediated the relationships between financial consumer protection, brand love, and brand advocacy. As an evolving concept in the global banking sector, financial consumer protection not only shapes consumer behaviour but also influences their trust and thus impacts branding advocacy efforts. This study fills the gap in the literature on the impact of financial consumer protection on branding by examining the influence of financial customer protection on brand love and brand advocacy. This research adds value to the branding literature by identifying new inter-construct relationships. It also contributes to the advancement of knowledge by exploring a novel construct (financial consumer protection). Understanding the role of financial consumer protection in brand love and brand advocacy can help bank practitioners to design branding strategies that support long-term profitability.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Contemporary digital marketing techniques used in unhealthy food campaigns targeting young people
hot.abstract: The digital marketing of unhealthy foods and non-alcoholic beverages has a detrimental impact on children's eating behaviours, leading to adverse diet-related health outcomes. To inform the development of evidence-based strategies to protect children online, this study aimed to describe contemporary digital marketing techniques and industry reported impacts from unhealthy food and beverage marketing campaigns aimed at young people aged 3-17. We conducted a qualitative conceptual content analysis of 111 industry reports detailing the nature and impact of unhealthy food and beverage marketing campaigns from around the world that directly or indirectly targeted children through digital channels. We categorised and narratively describe how food and beverage companies are using digital marketing techniques, across four conceptual groups: (i) leveraging data and technology to optimise marketing, (ii) profiling and segmenting audiences, (iii) targeting and personalisation, and (iv) generating participation and engagement. Industry reported impacts on young people as a result of campaigns included i) increased exposure to, and engagement with, unhealthy food marketing, ii) purchases and consumption of unhealthy foods and beverages iii) formation of emotional brand connections and enhanced future marketing through data collection. Our findings support and extend existing literature revealing how multinational food and beverage companies are using advanced digital marketing techniques, including artificial intelligence and new technologies, to shape children's food behaviours and influence their diets worldwide. Policy actions are needed to protect children from the sophisticated digital marketing techniques used by the food and beverage industry.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The influence of brand experience on brand loyalty in the electronic commerce sector: the mediating effect of brand association and brand trust
hot.abstract: Businesses are increasingly focusing on brand experience due to its dual role in directly creating customer value and shaping customers’ perceptions of brand equity. This study investigates the impact of brand experience on brand equity in Vietnam’s e-commerce sector. Primary data were collected from respondents with prior online shopping experience on e-commerce platforms. The research identifies four critical dimensions of brand experience in e-commerce services: sensory, affective, intellectual, and behavioral experiences. These components positively influence brand equity, particularly in terms of brand association, brand trust, and brand loyalty. Moreover, the study confirms the mediating roles of brand association and brand trust in the relationships between affective experience and brand loyalty, intellectual experience and brand loyalty, and behavioral experience and brand loyalty. This research offers a valuable contribution to the literature on brand experience and brand equity, especially within the e-commerce context. Managerial implications are also provided to guide businesses in enhancing customer brand experiences and strengthening brand equity.

hot.title: Roles of logistics service quality in shaping generation Z customers’ repurchase intention and electronic word of mouth in E-commerce industry
hot.abstract: As e-commerce continues to reshape retail landscapes, logistics service quality (LSQ) has become a crucial determinant of customer trust, satisfaction, and long-term engagement. This study investigates the impact of logistics service quality (LSQ) dimensions on the behavioral intentions of Generation Z consumers within Vietnam's rapidly expanding e-commerce sector. The research focuses on how various LSQ factors-timeliness, personal contact quality, order accuracy, order condition, order discrepancy handling, and return convenience-affect trust and satisfaction, which subsequently influence repurchase intention and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM). A quantitative approach was employed, gathering data from 495 Generation Z consumers with prior online shopping experience. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was used to test the proposed model and its hypotheses. This study found that key LSQ attributes play a significant role in shaping both trust and satisfaction, which, in turn, drive repurchase intention and eWOM. However, the findings indicate that Generation Z's expectations for seamless logistics experiences vary across different service attributes. While factors such as order accuracy, order condition, and order discrepancy handling contribute to satisfaction, they do not necessarily build trust, highlighting the generation's high standards and perception of these aspects as fundamental rather than differentiating features. This study challenges traditional LSQ frameworks by highlighting the evolving expectations of digital-native consumers. It offers practical insights for e-commerce businesses, emphasizing the need for a strategic blend of technological efficiency, personalized interactions, and seamless post-purchase services to enhance c

latest.title: Relationship between Income Level and Price Sensitivity Among Consumers
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Abstract Price is one of the many factors that have an effect on the buying decisions of consumers. However, the impact of price on the decision-making process is quite dissimilar at various income levels. The current study seeks to understand the effects of consumer income levels on price sensitivity, in other words, how the financial standing of the consumer affects their perception of price and their willingness to pay for brands and buy generally. Specifically, the research aims to examine the degree of price responsiveness among people of different income levels. The primary data for the study will be collected through the means of a structured survey of consumers of various income levels. The use of descriptive statistics and correlation analysis, among other statistical measures, will be required in the examination of the effects of income on price sensitivity. Finally, the overall goal of this research is to shed light on the effects of income on price sensitivity. Such information is extremely helpful for business organizations in creating appropriate price strategies. This study looks at how a person's income shapes how sensitive they are to price changes. Price sensitivity is simply how much a customer's buying choices shift when a price goes up or down. When you look at how people shop, income is usually the biggest piece of the puzzle. It determines what someone can actually afford, which naturally shapes how much they’re willing—and able—to hand over at the register. How you react to a price change often comes down to your bank account. When money is tight, every single dollar counts. You automatically become more cautious—you check price tags twice, hunt for coupons, and hold off on buying until things go on sale. When you have a comfortable financial cus

latest.title: PENGARUH CURRENT RATIO, PRICE TO BOOK VALUE DAN RETURN ON ASSET TERHADAP RETURN SAHAM
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Current Ratio (CR), Price to Book Value (PBV), and Return on Assets (ROA) on stock returns in telecommunication sub-sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The background of this study is based on fluctuations in companies' financial performance, which are assumed to influence the level of returns obtained by investors. The research method used is quantitative with an associative approach. The population consists of 22 telecommunication sub-sector companies, with a sample of 3 companies selected using purposive sampling technique. The research data includes 18 observations during the period 2019–2024. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with the help of SPSS version 26, including classical assumption tests, regression analysis, coefficient of determination test, t-test, and F-test. The results show that partially, CR and ROA have no significant effect on stock returns, with significance values of 0.506 and 0.316, respectively. Meanwhile, PBV has a significant effect on stock returns with a significance value of 0.044. Simultaneously, CR, PBV, and ROA do not have a significant effect on stock returns (Sig. 0.144). The coefficient of determination (R²) is 0.312, indicating that 31.2% of stock return variation can be explained by the model, while 68.8% is influenced by other factors outside the research model.

latest.title: From Free to Paid: Public Attitude Change and Mechanism Evidence around Doubao's Charging Announcement
latest.abstract: As generative AI moves from free access to paid subscription, how charging shapes public attitude bears on platform commercialization. Taking Doubao's monthly subscription as the setting, this paper builds a dual-path framework of “product experience - price perception”. Using the announcement date (May 4, 2026) as the breakpoint, we collect public Weibo discussions from 30 days before to 30 days after it (2-day periods; the 14 days on each side form the main window), measure attitude with aspect-based sentiment analysis, and test changes at the breakpoint by regression discontinuity in time. Negative evaluation is robust in direction for Payment Willingness (τ = +0.751, p < 0.001) and Corporate Brand (τ = +0.647, p = 0.011), but rests on only 27 and 7 pre-breakpoint texts, so the magnitudes are read as direction only. The negative share for Price & Charging shows no significant increase (τ = -0.161, p = 0.123), so the price-fairness path is not supported. The difference between the two aspect jumps is -0.532 (clustered SE 0.437, p = 0.245), opposite to expectation and underpowered given the small pre-breakpoint sample; we report only that no larger negative change was found for the price path than for the feature path. The overall negative share rises by 0.317 (p = 0.041) but depends on a pre-breakpoint period with 3 relevant texts and falls to 0.043 (p = 0.517) without it, so it is not robustly supported. The conclusions are limited to a marked change in attitude, with no persistent shift and no strict causal claim.

latest.title: Purchase Intention Formation for K-Beauty Cosmetics: The Mediating Role of Sensory Expectation and the Moderated Mediation of Cosmetic Involvement
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of consumers’ perception of K-beauty cosmetics in the digital consumption environment on purchase intention and to examine the mediating effect of sensory expectation and the moderated mediation effect of cosmetic involvement. An online survey was conducted from April 1 to April 28, 2026, with 305 Korean women aged 20–49 years. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS 30.0 and Hayes’ PROCESS Macro. Exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, multiple regression analysis, mediation analysis (Model 4), moderation analysis (Model 1), and moderated mediation analysis (Model 7) were performed. The results indicated that quality perception, price perception, and brand image all had significant positive effects on purchase intention, with quality perception showing the strongest effect. Sensory expectation partially mediated the relationships between quality perception, price perception, and brand image and purchase intention, while cosmetic involvement significantly moderated the relationships between each of these perception dimensions and purchase intention. Furthermore, moderated mediation analysis revealed that only the indirect effect of price perception on purchase intention through sensory expectation significantly varied according to the level of cosmetic involvement, with the indirect effect decreasing as cosmetic involvement increased. No significant moderated mediation effects were found for quality perception or brand image. These findings demonstrate that sensory expectation and cosmetic involvement play important roles in consumers’ purchase decision-making process in the digital consumption environment. latest.title: Hubungan Pemanfaatan Riwayat Transaksi QRIS dan Disiplin Pencatatan Keuangan dengan Pengelolaan Modal Kerja UMKM Kuliner Soppeng
latest.abstract: Digitalisasi pembayaran menyediakan riwayat transaksi yang dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai informasi keuangan, tetapi penggunaan QRIS belum tentu disertai pencatatan usaha yang disiplin. Penelitian ini menganalisis hubungan pemanfaatan riwayat transaksi QRIS dan disiplin pencatatan keuangan dengan praktik pengelolaan modal kerja UMKM kuliner di Kabupaten Soppeng. Data berasal dari kuesioner lapangan atas 120 responden yang disediakan peneliti. Variabel diukur menggunakan empat butir QRIS, lima butir pencatatan keuangan, dan lima butir pengelolaan modal kerja pada skala 1–5. Skor komposit dihitung dari jawaban tersedia; 18 responden memiliki satu jawaban item kosong. Analisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda dengan galat baku robust HC3 dan uji sensitivitas kasus lengkap. Reliabilitas Cronbach’s alpha untuk ketiga konstruk berkisar 0,817–0,854. Pemanfaatan riwayat transaksi QRIS (B = 0,2882; p = 0,0005) serta disiplin pencatatan keuangan (B = 0,4414; p < 0,001) berhubungan positif dengan pengelolaan modal kerja. Model menjelaskan 31,40% variasi skor pengelolaan modal kerja (R² = 0,3140). Hasil pada 102 responden lengkap menunjukkan arah hubungan yang sama. Temuan menekankan pentingnya pemanfaatan informasi transaksi sekaligus rutinitas pembukuan bagi pengelolaan dana operasional UMKM; desain potong lintang tidak membuktikan hubungan sebab-akibat

latest.title: The Effect of Niche Perfume Selection Attributes on the Consume Happiness: The Moderating Effect of Generation through Multi-Group Analysis
latest.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology
latest.abstract: Niche perfume has emerged as a mainstream segment of the perfume market, moving beyond mass-market offerings by reflecting Millennials and Generation Z’s strong preference for individuality and distinctive scent identities. This study aims to analyze the effects of niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. In addition, Millennials and Generation Z are proposed as a moderator affecting the niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. An online survey targeted Korean women from Millennials and Generation Z who have experience using niche perfume. A total of 296 survey responses were analyzed using structural equation modeling with AMOS 26.0 and SPSS 25.0. The results revealed that four key selection attributes emerged from the analysis: trend orientation, brand awareness, premium price perception, and scent. In addition, scent, brand awareness, and premium price perception had significant effects on consumer happiness. Furthermore, the moderating effect of generation was confirmed through multi-group analysis. Specifically, Among Millennials, trend orientation, brand awareness, and premium price perception influenced consumer happiness, whereas scent was the most influential factor among Generation Z. By identifying these causal relationships, this study contributes to expanding the advancement of research on niche perfume and provides implications for developing differentiated strategies tailored to generational characteristics of the Millennials and Generation Z.

latest.title: Market Dominance and Competitive Effects of Online Travel Platforms: A Case Study of Ctrip/Trip.com Group in China
latest.venue: Journal of Applied Economics and Social Dynamics
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of China’s digital economy has made online travel agencies (OTAs) an important intermediary between consumers and suppliers of accommodation, transport and tourism services. At the same time, platform concentration, network effects and contractual restrictions can create substantial market power. This study examines Ctrip and its parent, Trip.com Group, as a case through which to evaluate the formation and competitive effects of platform dominance. The analysis combines publicly available industry and corporate data with a June 2026 consumer questionnaire. It also incorporates a factual update based on the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) decision of July 2026. The revised analysis finds strong evidence that Trip.com Group has substantial market power, particularly in online hotel-booking platform services, but it avoids treating broad OTA gross merchandise value (GMV) shares as a legally sufficient measure of dominance. The platform’s scale can generate efficiencies through matching, standardisation, service quality and investment in digital infrastructure; however, dominance may also facilitate exclusionary contracting and restrictions on hotel pricing. The consumer survey suggests high brand salience and potential switching behaviour, but its non-probability sample and several instrument inconsistencies prevent causal or population-level inference. Overall, the evidence supports a balanced view: platform scale can improve coordination and consumer convenience, while competition policy remains necessary where contractual or algorithmic mechanisms restrict merchant autonomy or foreclose rivals.

latest.title: Inovasi Produk terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen: Studi Deskriptif Kualitatif pada Departemen Yakult Lady PT Yakult Indonesia Persada Cabang Bandung 2
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis peran inovasi produk terhadap keputusan pembelian konsumen pada Departemen Yakult Lady PT Yakult Indonesia Persada Cabang Bandung 2, dengan fokus pada produk Yakult Less Sugar dan Yakult Rasa Mangga. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif, informan terdiri atas 15 Yakult Lady dan 15 konsumen/calon konsumen, kedua kelompok informan memberikan informasi mengenai Yakult Less Sugar dan Yakult Rasa Mangga. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui tahapan pengumpulan data, reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan dan verifikasi kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kedua inovasi mampu meningkatkan perhatian dan ketertarikan konsumen, tetapi memiliki tingkat penerimaan yang berbeda. Yakult Less Sugar mendapat respons positif terutama karena kandungan gula yang lebih rendah, namun persepsi harga yang lebih tinggi menjadi salah satu kendala dalam mendorong pembelian ulang. Sementara itu, Yakult Rasa Mangga memperoleh penerimaan yang lebih kuat karena menawarkan rasa yang enak, segar, dan berbeda dari produk sebelumnya. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa inovasi produk berperan sebagai salah satu stimulus dalam keputusan pembelian, tetapi bukan merupakan satu-satunya faktor penentu. Faktor harga, selera, kebutuhan, promosi, kebiasaan konsumsi, dan daya beli turut memengaruhi keputusan konsumen.

latest.title: An Empirical Analysis of Factors Influencing Brand Equity in Coffee Shops: A Study of Jakarta, Indonesia
latest.venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of the coffee shop industry in Jakarta is a direct consequence of Indonesia’s strong contribution to global coffee production as the world’s fourth-largest coffee producer. The number of coffee shops in Indonesia has reached 10,000 outlets. Due to increased competition among coffee shops, businesses are offering better service quality, innovative products, and improved ambiance and atmosphere to enhance brand loyalty, which eventually contributes to brand equity. However, limited studies have investigated the brand equity factors of coffee shop brands in Jakarta, despite the intense market competition among them. This study investigates how various brand-related factors, such as brand awareness, perceived quality, brand association, and brand loyalty, influence the overall brand equity of coffee shop brands in this highly competitive market. This study adopted a descriptive, explorative, and cross-sectional design with quantitative methods to analyze data collected from a representative sample of coffee shop consumers in Jakarta. Data were collected from 390 respondents from Jakarta city of Indonesia from 390 respondents from Jakarta, Indonesia, and were analyzed using SmartPLS. The statistical analysis confirms that there is a significant relationship between the four factors and brand equity, with perceived quality being the most influential factor among the study variables. This study provides strategic managerial recommendations for coffee shop businesses in Jakarta to enhance brand equity, underscoring the vital role of superior perceived quality while supporting sustainable business growth.

latest.title: Pengaruh Pilihan Produk, Kelengkapan Produk dan Store Atmosphere Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Emas (Studi Kasus PT. Pegadaian UPC William Iskandar)
latest.abstract: Data nasabah emas pada PT Pegadaian UPC William Iskandar berfluktuasi selama 2022–2025, dan prasurvei menunjukkan pilihan produk yang terbatas, stok yang sering kosong, serta ruang pelayanan yang kurang nyaman. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh pilihan produk, kelengkapan produk, dan store atmosphere terhadap keputusan pembelian emas. Desain kuantitatif asosiatif diterapkan pada 108 nasabah yang dipilih dengan accidental sampling; ukuran sampel ditentukan dengan rumus Slovin (e = 10%) dari 752 nasabah dan ditambah sekitar 20%. Data kuesioner skala Likert lima poin dianalisis dengan uji asumsi klasik dan regresi linear berganda menggunakan SPSS 26. Pilihan produk (B = 0,343; β = 0,274; p = 0,001), kelengkapan produk (B = 0,391; β = 0,334; p < 0,001), dan store atmosphere (B = 0,394; β = 0,383; p < 0,001) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel signifikan (F = 443,563 > F tabel 2,69; p < 0,001; adjusted R² = 0,925). Unit layanan perlu menjaga ketersediaan ukuran emas yang dibutuhkan nasabah dan meningkatkan kenyamanan ruang pelayanan.

latest.title: The Influence of Perceived Authenticity and Local Food Image on Purchase Intention toward Local Culinary Products in Ambon City, Indonesia
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi dan Kewirausahaan West Science
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of perceived authenticity and local food image on purchase intention toward local culinary products in Ambon City, Indonesia. Local culinary products represent the cultural identity and gastronomic heritage of Maluku, yet consumers’ purchase intentions may depend on how they perceive the authenticity and overall image of these products. This study employed a quantitative approach involving 120 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using SPSS, including validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression. The correlation results indicate that perceived authenticity is positively associated with purchase intention ((r = 0.413), (p < 0.001)), while local food image demonstrates a stronger positive association with purchase intention ((r = 0.506), (p < 0.001)). Perceived authenticity and local food image are also positively correlated ((r = 0.296), (p = 0.001)). Furthermore, the regression model is statistically significant overall ((F = 29.074), (p < 0.001)) and explains 33.2% of the variation in purchase intention ((R^2 = 0.332)). These findings highlight the relevance of authenticity and local food image in understanding consumer purchase intentions. The study provides insights for local culinary businesses in Ambon to strengthen product authenticity, communicate cultural identity, and develop a favorable image of regional cuisine.

latest.title: When Temporal Features Reuse Data: Adjacent-Window Bias in Customer Panels
latest.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
latest.abstract: Customer histories are often converted into rolling or adjacent-window features for segmentation and prediction. The same period-level estimate may then appear as an outcome in one panel row and as a predictor in the next, creating apparent dynamics even when no carryover exists. We develop and apply a validation framework combining a no-carryover benchmark, fully disjoint temporal construction, an identical-sample estimator comparison and strict temporal holdout testing. The application uses 102 weeks of grocery transactions and 9,014 household-category relationships observed under both adjacent and disjoint designs. On this identical sample, the adjacent estimator implies a 1.78-percentage-point movement toward full-price purchasing for a 10-point increase in promotional share, whereas the fully disjoint estimator implies a 1.40-point movement in the opposite direction. A 36-cell Monte Carlo grid shows that adjacent estimators can remain positive under zero carryover across panel lengths and event frequencies, while disjoint estimators recover the null; under true persistence, adjacent construction attenuates or reverses the expected sign. Recent promotional share adds only .0063 to holdout AUC. The study shows that temporal feature validation must distinguish predictive usefulness from dynamic interpretation and intervention. The proposed audit supports model governance by identifying when customer-history features are informative for forecasting but unsafe for behavioural or policy claims.

latest.title: The Effect of Price Perception, Service Quality, and Social Media Promotion on Repurchase Intention
latest.venue: Jurnal Manajemen Pemasaran dan Perilaku Konsumen.
latest.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to examine the effects of price perception, service quality, and social media promotion on repurchase intention at Toko Berkah Jaya Celaket. Design/Methodology/Approach – The study employed a quantitative explanatory research approach to examine the relationships among the research variables. Using saturated sampling, all 56 customers who had made repeat purchases from the store were selected as respondents. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and hypothesis testing with SPSS Version 26, following instrument and classical assumption tests. Findings – The findings indicate that perceived price, service quality, and social media marketing have positive and significant effects on repurchase intention. These results suggest that improvements in customers’ price perceptions, service quality, and social media promotion can contribute to higher repurchase intention. Originality/Value – The study provides practical insight into strategies for maintaining the competitiveness and sustainability of traditional micro-enterprises. Its originality lies in providing empirical evidence on the combined effects of price perception, service quality, and social media marketing within the context of a traditional grocery store, a setting that is relatively overlooked in broader retail research. The findings emphasize the importance of these factors as survival strategies for traditional retailers facing increasing competition.

latest.title: From price image to online retailer loyalty: The role of trust and consumer sugrophobia
latest.abstract: This study introduces and explores sugrophobia, which is the fear of being deceived or exploited in transactions, as a key but underexplored concept influencing online shopping behavior.Sugrophobia reflects emotional discomfort stemming from self-blame and suspicion, motivating self-protective behavior.Data is collected from 600 consumers.The research hypotheses were analyzed by K-Means Cluster Analysis and SEM.As a result it was found that high sugrophobes display greater scepticism but also exhibit stronger loyalty once trust is established.Conversely, low sugrophobes are less sceptical and more responsive to price promotions.The findings reveal that trust is the primary driver of loyalty for high sugrophobes, whereas price image and trust jointly influence loyalty among low sugrophobes.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan, Suasana Kafe dan Kualitas Produk Terhadap Kepuasan Pelanggan Pada Rahasia Coffee Marelan
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh kualitas pelayanan, suasana kafe, dan kualitas produk terhadap kepuasan pelanggan Rahasia Coffee Marelan, coffee shop yang mengalami penurunan penjualan. Penelitian kuantitatif asosiatif ini melibatkan 115 pelanggan yang dipilih dengan purposive sampling, yaitu pelanggan berusia minimal 17 tahun yang pernah berkunjung dan bersedia mengisi kuesioner. Jumlah sampel ditentukan dengan rumus Lemeshow karena ukuran populasi tidak diketahui. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert lima poin dan dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda, uji t, dan uji F. Kualitas pelayanan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan (B = 0,218; p = 0,002), suasana kafe tidak berpengaruh signifikan (B = 0,066; p = 0,470), dan kualitas produk berpengaruh positif dan signifikan (B = 0,246; p < 0,001). Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berpengaruh signifikan (F = 115,462; p < 0,001) dan menjelaskan 75,1% variasi kepuasan pelanggan (Adjusted R² = 0,751). Kualitas produk memiliki koefisien terstandar terbesar (β = 0,503). Pengelola kafe perlu memprioritaskan konsistensi rasa dan penyajian, kemudian kecepatan serta keramahan pelayanan, sedangkan pembenahan suasana kafe menjadi upaya pendukung.

latest.title: Sufficiency and fast fashion: how marketers respond to the call to ‘sell less’
latest.abstract: The growth-driven model of the fast fashion industry has intensified environmental and social concerns, prompting calls for sufficiency-oriented marketing. Yet, research remains limited on how marketers navigate such demands within volume-driven organisations. This study examines how marketers engaged in fast fashion practice navigate sufficiency within volume-driven business models. In-depth interviews conducted with 19 marketers reveal a double bind, where supporting sufficiency risks professional credibility, while growth compliance generates moral discomfort. Marketers respond by employing self-protective strategies such as working within the system, consoling the self, outright rejection, and moral and physical distancing to preserve professional and moral identity. The study contributes to the micro-foundations of institutional theory by showing how marketers use moral and identity work to navigate competing demands within South Africa’s socio-economic context.

latest.title: The Influence of Room Prices on Millennials' Purchase Intention at the Intercontinental Bali Sanur Resort
authors: I Gusti Agung Ngurah Aksamalika Putra Pinatih
latest.abstract: The decline in website visits, room occupancy rates, and the proportion of millennial guests at the InterContinental Bali Sanur Resort highlights the need to examine factors associated with purchase intention. This study aims to analyze the relationship between price perception and millennials’ purchase intention at the resort. A quantitative survey was conducted involving 100 millennial respondents born between 1981 and 1996 who had accessed information about the resort through Google and had never stayed there. Data were collected through questionnaires and documentation and analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, simple linear regression, hypothesis testing, and the coefficient of determination. The results indicate that price perception is positively and significantly associated with purchase intention, with an unstandardized regression coefficient of 0.725, a t-value of 11.298, and a significance level of p < 0.001. The coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.566 indicates that the regression model explains 56.6% of the variation in purchase intention. These findings suggest that favorable perceptions of affordability, price competitiveness, and price suitability relative to benefits and service quality are associated with higher purchase intention among the respondents. Therefore, the resort should maintain competitive pricing and communicate the value of its products and services more effectively to prospective millennial customers.

latest.title: Persepsi Nilai Ekonomis dan Biaya Nonmoneter dalam Pembelian Produk PT Nissin Biscuit Indonesia
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis bagaimana konsumen mengungkapkan manfaat ekonomis dan pengorbanan nonmoneter dalam pengalaman pembelian produk Nissin di Nissin Café & Emporium, Ungaran. Penelitian menggunakan analisis konten kualitatif terarah terhadap 120 transkripsi ulasan Google Maps dengan kategori manfaat dan pengorbanan berdasarkan teori customer perceived value. Korpus mencakup 50 ulasan yang telah diverifikasi secara manual oleh tim peneliti serta 70 transkripsi tambahan yang dokumentasi sumber individualnya masih perlu dilengkapi. Pengkodean awal menemukan 17 komentar mengenai harga menarik, 18 mengenai kesepadanan harga dan manfaat, 24 mengenai variasi produk, dan delapan mengenai antrean kasir. Sebanyak 36 ulasan memuat sedikitnya satu manfaat, sedangkan 26 ulasan memuat pengorbanan layanan. Hanya enam ulasan menyebut keduanya dalam satu komentar. Sebagian besar pengalaman campuran mempertemukan manfaat produk dan ketidaknyamanan kunjungan, bukan secara eksplisit menunjukkan kesediaan menukar waktu tunggu dengan penghematan uang. Temuan menegaskan pentingnya memisahkan penghematan yang dipersepsikan, kegunaan produk, biaya transaksi, dan biaya kunjungan yang lebih luas. Penelitian tidak mengukur selisih harga aktual, nilai moneter waktu, hubungan kausal, ataupun kinerja keuangan perusahaan.

latest.title: Pengaruh Inovasi Layanan, Penanganan Keluhan dan Harga Terhadap Kepuasan Pelanggan Bunda Purwati Laundry Martubung
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh inovasi layanan, penanganan keluhan, dan harga terhadap kepuasan pelanggan Bunda Purwati Laundry Martubung, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian kuantitatif asosiatif ini melibatkan 100 pelanggan yang dipilih secara purposive, yaitu pelanggan yang telah menggunakan jasa minimal dua kali dan mengetahui layanan yang diberikan. Data dikumpulkan dengan kuesioner skala Likert lima poin yang telah diuji validitas dan reliabilitasnya, lalu dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda menggunakan SPSS 22. Harga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan pelanggan (t = 2,769; p = 0,007), sedangkan inovasi layanan (t = 0,970; p = 0,334) dan penanganan keluhan (t = 1,657; p = 0,101) tidak berpengaruh signifikan secara parsial. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berpengaruh signifikan (F = 5,889; p = 0,001), tetapi hanya menjelaskan 15,5% variasi kepuasan pelanggan. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa persepsi pelanggan tentang keterjangkauan, kesesuaian harga dengan kualitas, dan daya saing harga paling berkaitan dengan kepuasan, sedangkan peran inovasi layanan dan penanganan keluhan belum terbukti secara statistik. Pemilik usaha laundry dapat memprioritaskan kewajaran harga sambil memastikan keluhan diselesaikan tuntas dan inovasi layanan benar-benar dirasakan pelanggan.

latest.title: ANALISIS PENGARUH KUALITAS LAYANAN DAN KUALITAS PRODUK TERHADAP PERSEPSI HARGA DAN KEPUASAN KONSUMEN PADA RESTORAN CEPAT SAJI PT XYZ DI JAKARTA BARAT
latest.venue: Journal of Social and Economics Research
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh kualitas layanan dan kualitas produk terhadap persepsi harga dan kepuasan konsumen, serta menguji peran persepsi harga sebagai variabel mediasi pada restoran cepat saji PT XYZ di wilayah Jakarta Barat. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain kausalitas dan explanatory research. Data diperoleh melalui kuesioner tertutup berskala Likert lima poin dari 245 responden yang dipilih menggunakan purposive sampling. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan bantuan SmartPLS. Hasil evaluasi model pengukuran menunjukkan seluruh indikator yang dipertahankan memenuhi kriteria validitas dan reliabilitas. Nilai HTMT seluruh pasangan konstruk berada di bawah 0,90. Pada model struktural, kualitas layanan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap persepsi harga dan kepuasan konsumen. Kualitas produk juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap persepsi harga dan kepuasan konsumen. Persepsi harga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan konsumen. Selain itu, persepsi harga terbukti memediasi pengaruh kualitas layanan dan kualitas produk terhadap kepuasan konsumen. Nilai R² sebesar 0,708 untuk persepsi harga dan 0,813 untuk kepuasan konsumen menunjukkan bahwa model memiliki kemampuan penjelasan yang kuat terhadap kedua variabel endogen. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengalaman konsumen terhadap kualitas produk, kualitas layanan, dan kewajaran harga perlu dikelola secara terpadu dalam meningkatkan kepuasan konsumen PT XYZ.

latest.title: Pengaruh Citra Rasa, Variasi Menu dan Fasilitas Kafe terhadap Loyalitas Pelanggan pada Romansakopii Marelan
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh citra rasa, variasi menu, dan fasilitas kafe terhadap loyalitas pelanggan Romansakopii Marelan, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian kuantitatif ini melibatkan 100 pelanggan yang dipilih dengan purposive sampling, yaitu pelanggan berusia minimal 17 tahun yang telah berkunjung minimal dua kali dan bersedia mengisi kuesioner. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner skala Likert dan dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda. Citra rasa (β = 0,317; p = 0,002), variasi menu (β = 0,429; p < 0,001), dan fasilitas kafe (β = 0,211; p = 0,036) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap loyalitas pelanggan. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berpengaruh signifikan (F = 185,189; p < 0,001) dan menjelaskan 85,3% variasi loyalitas pelanggan (R² = 0,853). Variasi menu memiliki koefisien terstandar terbesar, sehingga perluasan pilihan menu, termasuk penyediaan menu makanan, perlu menjadi prioritas pengelola kafe, disertai upaya menjaga konsistensi rasa serta memperbaiki tata ruang dan fasilitas pendukung. Temuan ini juga menunjukkan bahwa variasi menu berperan dalam loyalitas pelanggan kafe, berbeda dengan sebagian penelitian terdahulu.

latest.title: IMPACT OF PRICE SENSITIVITY ON CONSUMERS’ DECISION-MAKING IN AIRLINE TICKET PURCHASES
latest.venue: Journal of Global Peace-Marketing and Communications (JGPMC)
latest.abstract: This research examines how price sensitivity shapes consumers’ decisions when purchasing airline tickets in Calabar, Cross River State. Its specific focus is on the role of alternative evaluation and sensitivity to booking time. Two null hypotheses were tested: that neither alternative evaluation nor booking-time sensitivity significantly influences ticket-purchase decisions. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, covering passengers travelling to different destinations through Margaret Ekpo International Airport. Stratified sampling was used to allocate the 400 respondents among Ibom Air, Cally Air and Air Peace. Primary data were obtained with a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, means and standard deviations) and multiple linear regression. The findings show that respondents placed the greatest emphasis on promotional deals and discounts when comparing fares (mean = 4.58), while booking early to obtain cheaper tickets was the highest-rated booking-time behaviour (mean = 3.74). Regression results indicate statistically significant effects for alternative evaluation (p = 0.004) and booking-time sensitivity (p = 0.002), both below the 0.05 threshold. The study concludes that comparing available options and choosing booking times carefully can influence ticket-purchase decisions. Airlines are therefore encouraged to review pricing arrangements and strengthen appropriate discount and promotional programmes to attract and retain customers. Keywords: Airline Ticket Purchases, Alternative Evaluation, Booking Time Sensitivity, Price Sensitivity, Consumers’ Decision-Making.

latest.title: The Impact of Cashless Payment Adoption on Impulsive Spending Behavior Among Generation Z: Empirical Evidence from Vietnam
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructures and e-wallets has fundamentally altered consumer transaction habits, particularly among digital natives. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and mental accounting theory, this study investigates the empirical impact of cashless payment adoption on the impulsive spending behavior of Generation Z consumers in Vietnam. A quantitative survey was administered to 320 Gen Z respondents across major metropolitan areas, utilizing a 5-point Likert scale. Multiple linear regression and reliability tests were deployed to evaluate the proposed hypotheses. The empirical findings reveal that perceived convenience, promotional incentives, and subjective social norms exhibit a statistically significant positive effect on spending frequency and impulsive purchasing. Notably, the reduction in the psychological 'pain of paying' significantly diminishes financial self-control among younger cohorts. Based on these insights, the paper proposes actionable recommendations for higher education institutions, fintech platforms, and policymakers to foster financial literacy.

latest.title: The Influence of Brand Trust, Price Perception, and Customer Experience on Tomoro Coffee Cirebon Customer Loyalty
latest.abstract: The internalization of fiqh values at MAN Insan Cendekia Serpong, South Tangerang City, was implemented through three interconnected stages: value transformation, value transaction, and value transinternalization. Value transformation involved delivering instructional content on worship and muamalah through lectures, discussions, question-and-answer sessions, and practical activities. Value transaction emphasized active teacher–student interactions to strengthen students' understanding and appreciation of religious values, while value transinternalization involved applying these values through consistent habituation in school and dormitory environments. Student character formation was supported by continuous instruction and habituation, reflected in religious commitment, discipline, honesty, responsibility, and respectful conduct. These characteristics were demonstrated through congregational worship, compliance with school regulations, and respectful interactions with teachers and peers. The findings suggested that fiqh instruction contributed to character formation by integrating moral knowing, moral feeling, and moral action, thereby extending beyond knowledge transmission to support students' moral and religious development. However, the internalization process varied among students and required sustained reinforcement through teacher role modeling, habituation, and institutional support.Based on these findings, teachers are encouraged to adopt varied, contextual, and reflective instructional strategies, integrate digital technology appropriately, reinforce positive behavioral changes, and conduct continuous character assessments. latest.title: The Price of Pocket Money
latest.abstract: Adolescent consumption lies at the intersection of behavioural economics, developmental psychology and consumer research. Although conventional economic models explain consumer choice through preferences, prices and budget constraints, actual purchasing decisions may also be shaped by cognitive biases, emotional responses, peer influence and the perceived origin of money. This study examines the relationship between adolescents’ income sources and impulsive spending, with attention to parental allowances, monetary gifts, family transfers and personal earnings. Its theoretical framework draws on mental accounting, the house-money effect, psychological ownership and the pain of paying, while also considering parental financial practices, digital payments, social commerce and targeted advertising. The research uses a quantitative primary-research approach based on survey responses collected from more than 500 teenagers. The survey provides first-hand material for examining adolescents’ money sources and spending behaviour; published research is used to contextualise the topic and interpret the possible mechanisms behind consumer decisions. The paper does not assume that earned income necessarily leads to responsible spending or that unearned income inevitably produces impulsive purchases. Instead, it considers how income origin may interact with financial responsibility, perceived scarcity, budgeting practices and the contemporary consumption environment. The study’s conclusions and recommendations are framed with due regard to the limits of survey-based evidence and the need to distinguish observed associations from causal explanations.

latest.title: PENGARUH PRODUCT QUALITY, CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE TERHADAP CUSTOMER SATISFACTION DAN CUSTOMER LOYALTY DIMODERASI OLEH BRAND IMAGE PADA PRODUK SKINCARE
latest.abstract: Industri kecantikan di Indonesia saat ini berkembang pesat karena kebutuhan masyarakat, terutama wanita, untuk merawat diri dan gaya hidup yang berkembang pesat. Penelitian ini untuk melihat bagaimana customer satisfaction dan customer loyalty Skintific di Jabodetabek dipengaruhi oleh product quality dan customer experience. Di sisi lain, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk melihat bagaimana brand image berfungsi sebagai moderasi dalam hubungan antara customer satisfaction dan customer loyalty Skintific di Jabodetabek. Metode penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif. Populasi yang akan diteliti adalah pelanggan Skintific di Jabodetabek. Selanjutnya, pengambilan sampel dilakukan dengan metode purposive non-probability sampling. Sampel penelitian sebanyak 130 responden. Metode analisis data dengan Structural Partial Least Square Equation Model (SEM-PLS). Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa product quality, customer experience mempengaruhi customer satisfaction dan customer loyalty secara positif. Selain itu hasil penelitian membuktikan bahwa customer satisfaction berpengaruh terhadap customer loyalty secara positif. Di lain sisi brand image tidak dapat memoderasi customer satisfaction dengan customer loyalty. Penelitian ini diharapkan mampu membantu pihak Skintific untuk meningkatkan produk, layanan, dan strategi mereka secara keseluruhan, yang pada akhirnya mendukung pertumbuhan bisnis dan kesuksesan jangka panjang

latest.title: ИЛЛЮЗИЯ БЕСПЛАТНЫХ ДЕНЕГ: ОТ BNPL К КРЕДИТНЫМ КАРТАМ В ПОТРЕБИТЕЛЬСКОМ ПОВЕДЕНИИ МОЛОДЁЖИ УЗБЕКИСТАНА
latest.abstract: В статье рассматриваются продукты типа «купи сейчас - плати потом» (BNPL), которые предлагаются в Узбекистане на условиях «без процентов»: кредитные карты банков с беспроцентным периодом, рассрочка («Nasiya») и BNPL-микрозаймы. Исследование отвечает на вопрос: «где на самом деле находятся издержки, если реклама обещает ноль процентов, и как это влияет на потребительское поведение молодёжи?». Методология включает анализ международной и отечественной литературы, материалов Центрального банка Республики Узбекистан и сравнительный анализ публично раскрытых условий кредитных карт трёх банков (Hamkorbank, TBC Bank, SQB) по состоянию на октября 2026 года. Показано, что «беспроцентность» не означает отсутствия издержек: они смещаются в наценку на товар, комиссии за снятие наличных и переводы, штрафы и ставку после льготного периода, а накопление нескольких договоров формирует скрытую долговую нагрузку. Предложены концептуальная модель механизма «иллюзии бесплатных денег» и пакет рекомендаций по раскрытию полной стоимости, защите молодых заёмщиков и мониторингу рынка.

latest.title: THE EFFECT OF PRODUCT QUALITY AND SERVICE QUALITY ON CUSTOMER SATISFACTION WITH PRICE AS A MODERATING VARIABLE AT KALANI CAFE
latest.venue: International Journal of Economic Business Accounting Agriculture Management and Sharia Administration (IJEBAS)
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of product quality and service quality on customer satisfaction with price as a moderating variable at Kalani Cafe. Kalani Cafe is located on Jl. Batang Kuis, Bangun Sari Baru, Tanjung Morawa District, Deli Serdang Regency, North Sumatra. Kalani Cafe is characterized by its casual and trendy style, becoming a favorite gathering place for young people and community groups in the area. The sample selection method used was random sampling with the Slovin formula as the sample determination method. The total number of observations in this study was 100. The data analysis techniques used in this study were multiple linear regression analysis and moderation analysis. The results of simultaneous testing indicate that product quality, service quality, and price simultaneously influence customer satisfaction. The results of partial testing indicate that product quality and service quality influence customer satisfaction. The results of the moderation test indicate that price is able to moderate and strengthen the influence of product quality on customer satisfaction, but does not moderate and weaken the influence of service quality on customer satisfaction.

latest.title: Zero price or token price? The impact of bundle promotional format on promotional attractiveness and value discounting
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the relative attractiveness of freebie (e.g. “buy one, get one free”) and token-price (e.g. “buy one, get the second one for only 1¢”) promotions in the short run and value discounting effect for the separate items in the long run. Design/methodology/approach Two imaginary-scenario and two incentive-compatible experiments test the hypotheses. Findings Token-price promotions are more attractive than freebie promotions no matter if the supplemental item is identical to the focal item or not. Moreover, when the two items are identical, consumers who encounter a token-price (vs freebie) promotion express stronger value discounting for the focal item. This effect reverses when the items are nonidentical. Research limitations/implications Future research should examine whether the bundle promotional format effect differs with the amount of the token price and the complementarity of the focal and supplemental items. Practical implications Practitioners can draw on the findings to determine when to use freebie or token-price promotions and how to adjust bundle promotional strategies according to the type of the supplemental item. Originality/value This study improves understanding of the effects of freebie and token-price promotions, especially over the long-term. Based on mental accounting theory, the authors build a comprehensive framework that explains how the bundle promotional format influences promotional attractiveness and value discounting.

latest.title: The Effects of Social Media Marketing and Price Fairness on Purchase Decisions through Purchase Intention on TikTok Shop
latest.abstract: This purposive online survey of 122 existing TikTok Shop buyers examines social media marketing, price fairness, purchase intention, and self-reported purchase decisions using SmartPLS 4. Five direct paths were positive and significant. Reported indirect effects were 0.098 (p = 0.023) for marketing and 0.092 (p = 0.048) for fairness; complementary partial mediation remains qualified pending bootstrap intervals. Explained variance was 52.7% for intention and 53.3% for decisions. Questionnaire associations do not establish transaction outcomes or temporal ordering. Informative content and transparent prices are contextual implications, not tested sales interventions.

latest.title: Service Quality and Premium Price Perception in Building Customer Loyalty: The Mediating Role of Satisfaction in Surety Bond Services
latest.venue: Siber International Journal of Digital Business (SIJDB)
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationships among service quality, premium price perception, customer satisfaction, and customer loyalty in business-to-business (B2B) Surety Bond services. The study was conducted at PT Asuransi Kredit Indonesia (PT Askrindo) Bandung Branch Office. A quantitative cross-sectional design was applied. Data were collected from 140 representatives of business entities or principals that had experience using Surety Bond services. Respondents were selected through purposive sampling, with one respondent representing one customer organization. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction (β=0.818, t=10.509,p<0.001). Customer satisfaction also has a positive and significant effect on customer loyalty (β=0.689, t=5.462,p<0.001). Furthermore, customer satisfaction significantly mediates the relationship between service quality and customer loyalty (β=0.563,t=4.521, p<0.001). In contrast, premium price perception does not significantly influence customer satisfaction or customer loyalty and does not have a significant indirect effect on loyalty through satisfaction. The findings suggest that customer loyalty in B2B Surety Bond services is primarily developed through reliable and satisfying service experiences rather than premium price evaluations alone. The study highlights the strategic importance of process accuracy, service responsiveness, information clarity, employee competence, document accuracy, and customer relationship management in strengthening retention within the Surety Bond business.

latest.title: Paradoks Buy Now, Pay Later Syariah dan Ketahanan Finansial Generasi Z
latest.venue: BALANCA Jurnal Ekonomi dan Bisnis Islam
latest.abstract: Sharia Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) services offer deferred payment under contracts oriented toward Sharia compliance, but the validity of the contract does not automatically prevent impulsive purchasing, installment accumulation, and the weakening of Generation Z’s financial resilience. This article aims to explain why formal Sharia compliance can be distant from users’ financial resilience, how Islamic financial literacy, self-control, and religiosity shape patterns of Sharia BNPL use, and what design and governance improvements are needed. The study uses an integrative literature review with PICOS-based eligibility criteria and the PRISMA 2020 selection flow; 33 sources were analyzed through thematic coding and conceptual synthesis from the perspective of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah. The results show three things. First, contract compliance guarantees the validity of transactions, but installment framing, promotions, and disproportionate limits can give rise to a Sharia Compliance–Financial Resilience Gap. Second, Islamic financial literacy protects users only when it is translated by self-control into postponing purchases, limiting installments, and payment discipline; substantive religiosity strengthens this pathway, whereas symbolic acceptance of the Sharia label (the Sharia label halo effect) can weaken risk evaluation. Third, sustainable Sharia BNPL requires affordability assessment, prominent display of total obligations, ethical friction, Sharia audits of interfaces and promotions, and simulation-based education. This article offers the Dual Pathway Model of Sustainable Sharia BNPL Behavior as a heuristic framework for subsequent empirical testing

latest.title: ความสมพนธระหวางหนครวเรอนกบการลงทนในสนทรพยทางการเงน: กรณศกษาบคลากรภาครฐของสำนกงานบรหารหนสาธารณะ
latest.venue: Journal of MCU Social Science Review
latest.abstract: The purposes of this research article were: 1. To examine investment behavior in financial assets, 2. To investigate household debt, 3. To analyze the relationship between household debt and financial asset investment, and 4. To analyze the relationship between personal factors and investment behavior among personnel at the Public Debt Management Office (PDMO). This study employed a quantitative research methodology, utilizing online questionnaires for data collection from a sample group of 160 respondents. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including frequency and percentage, alongside the Chi-Square Test of Independence. The findings revealed that: 1. 67.50% of personnel invested in financial assets, primarily mutual funds and government bonds, with low and irregular investment-to-income ratios; 2. 74.38% had debt obligations, mainly housing and credit card debts, maintaining low debt service ratios under 20%; 3. Overall debt obligations had no significant relationship with investment decisions (p-value = 0.750), but the debt service-to-income ratio, debt-to-asset ratio, and debt types were significantly related to the financial asset ratio at the 0.05 level, where debt service exceeding 40% resulted in the highest rate of non-investment; and 4. Personal factors (education, major, position, income, and expenses) were significantly related to investment behavior. This study synthesized a novel "PDMO-Financial Balance Model" highlighting a critical 40% debt service threshold impacting investment capacity.

latest.title: THE EFFECT OF PRODUCT QUALITY, PRICE AND PRODUCT DESIGN ON WOODEN DOOR PURCHASE DECISIONS AT PT. SUKSES MAKMUR TIGA ENAM TUJUH
latest.venue: Journal of Accounting Research Utility Finance and Digital Assets
latest.abstract: The increasingly competitive furniture industry requires companies to understand the factors influencing consumer purchasing decisions. PT. Sukses Makmur Tiga Enam Tujuh Medan, as a company engaged in wooden door manufacturing, faces challenges in maintaining market competitiveness due to changing consumer preferences regarding product quality, price, and product design. This study aims to analyze the effect of product quality, price, and product design on purchasing decisions for wooden doors at PT. Sukses Makmur Tiga Enam Tujuh Medan, both partially and simultaneously. This research employed a quantitative approach with an associative research method. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to consumers of PT. Sukses Makmur Tiga Enam Tujuh Medan. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression analysis, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination analysis. The results showed that product quality had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions with a t-value of 6.041 and a significance level of 0.000. Price also had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions with a t-value of 4.987 and a significance level of 0.000. Furthermore, product design had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions with a t-value of 4.053 and a significance level of 0.000. Simultaneously, product quality, price, and product design significantly influenced purchasing decisions with an F-value of 32.427 and an R Square value of 0.503. The novelty of this study lies in its comprehensive examination of three essential consumer value dimensions within the wooden door industry context. The findings reveal that product quality is the most dominant factor influencing consumer purchasing decisions compared to other variables. This r

latest.title: A Comparative Analysis of Price Fluctuations in Woodland, Bata and Campus Footwear on Amazon India and Flipkart during the 2026 Festive Sale Period
latest.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
latest.abstract: Online marketplaces make footwear prices easy to compare, but displayed prices can vary by model, variant, seller, availability, observation date, and promotional eligibility. This study examines available price evidence for selected Woodland, Bata, and Campus footwear listings on Amazon India and Flipkart during the 2026 festive-sale monitoring project. It adopts a quantitative, descriptive and observational design with a longitudinal orientation. The baseline frame includes 11 records, with 10 numeric prices ranging from ?629 to ?3,299; the mean is ?1,339.40, and the median is ?999. Two dated secondary tracker comparisons show lower later values: Campus Men First Running Shoes declined from ?1,291 on 4 October 2026 to ?999 on 11 October 2026, a difference of ?292 or 22.62%; Woodland men?s GC 6340024HS sneaker declined from ?2,789 on 31 August 2026 to ?2,138 on 15 October 2026, a difference of ?651 or 23.34%. These are endpoint comparisons, not complete daily observations or direct checkout records. The available evidence does not establish an exact same-date, same-product-and-variant price pair across Amazon India and Flipkart, a complete daily sale-period panel, or a causal effect of the festive sale. The article emphasizes product matching, consistent price definitions, and transparent reporting of missing evidence.

latest.title: Digital Payment and Spending Pattern: A Study among Young Consumers in Nepal
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationship between digital payment system (DPS) usage and spending pattern among 179 young Nepalese consumers, using a positivist, descriptive and causal-comparative research design with a cross-sectional time horizon, a quantitative approach, and convenience sampling. Data on five constructs Ease of Transactions, Financial Tracking, Rewards and Cashback, Bill Payment, and Spending Pattern were analysed using Kendall's tau_b correlation and multiple linear regression in SPSS. Respondents were predominantly young, female, and frequent DPS users. Ease of Transactions showed the strongest positive correlation with spending pattern, while Financial Tracking and Bill Payment showed no significant association. The regression model was significant, F(4,174) = 34.080, p < .001, explaining 43.9% of variance in spending pattern. Ease of Transactions was the strongest positive predictor (Beta = .695, p < .001), while Financial Tracking was a significant negative predictor (Beta = -.212, p = .003). No multicollinearity or autocorrelation was detected. Convenience is the primary driver of spending, while tracking tools appear to restrain it.

latest.title: The Influence of Digital Marketing and Digital Service Experience on Customer Loyalty Through Customer Trust: A Case Study of BRI Insurance
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of digital marketing and digital service experience on customer loyalty through customer trust at BRI Insurance Denpasar Branch. The increasing internet penetration and digital transformation in Indonesia's insurance industry urge companies to optimize digital-based marketing strategies to retain and enhance customer loyalty. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed, involving 120 active customers of BRI Insurance Denpasar Branch selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a 5-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 3.0. The results indicate that digital marketing has a positive and significant effect on customer trust (β = 0.412; p < 0.05), digital service experience has a positive and significant effect on customer trust (β = 0.358; p < 0.05), and customer trust has a positive and significant effect on customer loyalty (β = 0.524; p < 0.05). Customer trust is proven to partially mediate the relationship between digital marketing, digital service experience, and customer loyalty. These findings imply that BRI Insurance needs to integrate a consistent digital marketing strategy with improved digital service experience quality to strengthen long-term customer trust and loyalty. Keywords: Digital Marketing, Digital Service Experience, Customer Trust, Customer Loyalty, BRI Insurance.

latest.venue: Journal of Multidisciplinary in Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: This article aimed to 1) develop and validate a causal relationship model of purchasing behavior for dietary supplements on Facebook pages and 2) study the causal factors influencing such purchasing behavior. This study employed a quantitative research design. Data were collected using an online questionnaire administered to a sample of 326 respondents who had previously purchased dietary supplements via Facebook pages. Statistical techniques used for data analysis included frequency, percentage, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM). Findings revealed that the developed causal relationship model was highly consistent with the empirical data. The model comprised four key components: 1) perceived value, 2) product information, 3) satisfaction, and 4) purchasing behavior. Model fit indices indicated a satisfactory fit to the empirical data, with a chi-square/df (χ2/df) of 0.536, a goodness of fit index (GFI) of 0.983, an adjusted goodness of fit index (AGFI) of 0.968, and a root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) of 0.000. Furthermore, satisfaction (β=0.58, p=.001), product information (β=0.32, p=.001), and perceived price (β=0.27, p=.001) were found to have significant positive direct effects on dietary supplement purchasing behavior. Entrepreneurs should place emphasis on establishing appropriate pricing strategies and providing clear and comprehensive product information to enhance consumer satisfaction, which in turn can stimulate purchasing behavior for dietary supplements through Facebook pages.

latest.title: THE IMPACT OF BEHAVIORAL ECONOMICS ON FINANCIAL DECISION-MAKING AND SAVING BEHAVIOR IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: EMPIRICAL TRENDS AND POLICY IMPLICATIONS FROM UZBEKISTAN
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital financial services has transformed how individuals manage income, make payments, save money, and respond to financial incentives. This study examines the relationship between digital financial development and household financial behavior in Uzbekistan through the theoretical framework of behavioral economics. Particular attention is paid to present bias, mental accounting, financial self-control, loss aversion, and choice architecture. The research employs descriptive statistical analysis, comparative assessment, growth-rate calculations, structural ratio analysis, and scenario modeling based on official data published by the Central Bank of Uzbekistan. The findings indicate that funds credited to bank cards increased from UZS 789 trillion in 2023 to UZS 1,496 trillion in 2025, representing cumulative growth of approximately 89.6%. Meanwhile, the ratio of cash withdrawals to funds credited to bank cards declined from approximately 24.0% to 18.6%. Total banking system deposits increased from UZS 308.7 trillion at the beginning of 2025 to UZS 417.3 trillion at the beginning of 2026. These developments demonstrate significant changes in the financial environment in which consumers make payment and saving decisions. However, aggregate financial indicators do not establish whether digital financial services directly improve self-control or household saving behavior. The study develops a behavioral-financial framework and proposes digital interventions including automated saving options, expenditure feedback, financial goal-setting, and transparent choice architecture. The proposed measures aim to strengthen financial resilience and improve the quality of household financial decision-making.

hot.title: Psychology’s Theory Crisis, and why formal modelling cannot solve it
hot.abstract: In light of psychology’s ‘theory crisis’, multiple authors have argued that adopting formalization and/or formal modelling would constitute a useful or even necessary step towards stronger psychological theory. In this article, I instead argue that formal modelling cannot solve the core problem the psychological ‘theory crisis’ refers to, which are the currently high degrees of contrastive and holistic underdetermination of our theories by our data. I do so by first introducing underdetermination as an explanatory framework for determining the evidential import of research findings for theories, and showing how both broader theoretical considerations and informal assumptions are key to this process. Then, I derive the aforementioned core problem from the current ‘theory crisis’ literature and tentatively explore its possible solutions. Lastly, I show that formal modelling is neither a necessary nor sufficient solution for either contrastive or holistic underdetermination, and that its uncritical adoption might instead worsen the crisis.

hot.title: From Asymmetry to Satisfaction: The Dynamic Role of Perceived Value and Trust to Boost Customer Satisfaction in the Tourism Industry
hot.abstract: The study investigates how information asymmetry affects customer satisfaction in the tourism industry by examining trust and perceived value as mediating factors. The research implements an integrated model to test and prove information asymmetry’s direct and mediating effects on customer satisfaction by examining the literature gap. The research used a quantitative approach based on opinion polls distributed to 408 customers of hotels, tourism companies, and travel agencies who were in Egypt. SmartPLS 3 software implemented the data analysis process using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Previous studies have developed scales to measure information asymmetry and its related constructs, including customer trust, perceived value, and customer satisfaction. Multiple tests showed that the measurement tools possess both reliability and validity. Results strongly support all hypotheses: information asymmetry demonstrated significant direct negative effects on customer satisfaction (β = −0.187), trust (β = −0.520), and perceived value (β = −0.453). Conversely, customer satisfaction received significant positive direct effects from both trust (β = 0.273) and perceived value (β = 0.263). Importantly, trust (indirect effect β = −0.142) and perceived value (indirect effect β = −0.119) acted as powerful mediators, confirming that information asymmetry diminishes satisfaction largely by eroding these crucial factors. Crucially, the results demonstrate that the negative impact of information asymmetry on customer satisfaction is significantly mediated jointly through two parallel pathways: the erosion of customer trust and the impairment of perceived value. The research adds theoretical support to information asymmetry theory with its findings while als
